	return math.sqrt(8 * allowedError / magnitude)
end

-- Time until the current straight trajectory reaches the next chunk plane.
-- Sampling a nudge ahead resolves the ambiguous "exactly on a plane" case in
-- favor of the chunk the projectile is entering; the sample is a double, not
-- a Vector3, so the nudge survives at any distance from the origin.
function ProjectileMotion.GetChunkBoundaryDt(
	position: Vector3,
	velocity: Vector3,
	chunkSize: number,
	useY: boolean
): number
	local speed = velocity.Magnitude
	if not (speed >= EPSILON) then
		return math.huge
	end

	local nudge = ProjectileMotion.GetNudge(position)
	local best = math.huge

	local function consider(coordinate: number, velocityComponent: number)
		local directionComponent = velocityComponent / speed
		if math.abs(directionComponent) < EPSILON then
			return
		end
		local cell = math.floor((coordinate + directionComponent * nudge) / chunkSize)
		local boundary = if directionComponent > 0 then (cell + 1) * chunkSize else cell * chunkSize
		local dt = (boundary - coordinate) / velocityComponent
		if dt > 0 and dt < best then
			best = dt
		end
	end

	consider(position.X, velocity.X)
	consider(position.Z, velocity.Z)
	if useY then
		consider(position.Y, velocity.Y)
	end

	return best
end

-- Finds the first crossed chunk plane whose far side actually has a different
-- time scale. Equal-scale chunks are skipped, so very fast projectiles do not
-- pay one substep per 64 studs across ordinary 1x space.
function ProjectileMotion.GetTimeScaleBoundaryDt(
	position: Vector3,
	velocity: Vector3,
	chunkSize: number,
	useY: boolean,
	currentScale: number,
	maxDt: number,
	getScaleAt: (Vector3) -> number
): number
	local speed = velocity.Magnitude
	if not (speed >= EPSILON) then
		return math.huge
	end

	local direction = velocity / speed
	local cursorTime = 0
	for _ = 1, 32 do
		local cursorPosition = position + velocity * cursorTime
		local boundaryDt = ProjectileMotion.GetChunkBoundaryDt(cursorPosition, velocity, chunkSize, useY)
		if boundaryDt == math.huge then
			return math.huge
		end
		local boundaryTime = cursorTime + boundaryDt
		if boundaryTime >= maxDt then
			return math.huge
		end
		local boundaryPosition = position + velocity * boundaryTime
		local nudge = ProjectileMotion.GetNudge(boundaryPosition)
		if getScaleAt(boundaryPosition + direction * nudge) ~= currentScale then
			return boundaryTime
		end
		cursorTime = boundaryTime + nudge / speed
	end

	-- Bound the scan itself in pathological ultra-fast cases; the next
	-- simulation segment resumes the search from here without losing time.
	return cursorTime
end

return ProjectileMotion
-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/shared/ProjectileMotion.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/shared/ProjectileStepPlanner.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!native
--!strict
--!optimize 2
--[[
	ProjectileStepPlanner.luau
	Chooses the next integration substep for a projectile. The authoritative
	server Step and the client's dead-reckoning both call this, so they
	partition time identically: same chunk sampling, same boundary stops,
	same curvature limit, same carry rule for time too small to integrate.
	Keeping one copy is what keeps the two sides from drifting apart as
	either one is tuned.

	Per substep:
	 local sample, chunkScale = Planner.Sample(position, velocity, accel, uniformTime)
	 -- chunkScale == 0: frozen chunk; consume the frame's remaining time.
	 local stepDt = Planner.StepDt(position, velocity, accel, chunkScale,
	     remaining, lifeRemaining, nearEntities, uniformTime, maxDt)
	 -- stepDt == 0: not enough time for a meaningful step; carry `remaining`.

	Remaining time is in personal/global seconds (before chunk dilation); a
	step of stepDt dilated seconds consumes stepDt / chunkScale of it.
]]

local ChunkManager = require(script.Parent.ChunkManager)
local ProjectileMotion = require(script.Parent.ProjectileMotion)
local SafeMath = require(script.Parent.SafeMath)

local Planner = {}

-- Chunk/zone scale as projectile motion sees it -- see
-- ProjectileMotion.SnapTimeScale.
function Planner.ChunkTimeScaleAt(position: Vector3): number
	return ProjectileMotion.SnapTimeScale(ChunkManager.GetTimeScaleAt(position))
end

-- Returns a point just ahead of `position` along the direction of travel,
-- and the chunk time scale there (the chunk being entered wins when
-- sitting exactly on a boundary).
function Planner.Sample(
	position: Vector3,
	velocity: Vector3,
	accelerationVector: Vector3,
	uniformTime: boolean
): (Vector3, number)
	local direction = SafeMath.direction(velocity, SafeMath.direction(accelerationVector, Vector3.zAxis))
	local sample = position + direction * ProjectileMotion.GetNudge(position)
	return sample, if uniformTime then 1 else Planner.ChunkTimeScaleAt(sample)
end

function Planner.StepDt(
	position: Vector3,
	velocity: Vector3,
	accelerationVector: Vector3,
	chunkScale: number,
	remaining: number,
	lifeRemaining: number,
	nearEntities: boolean,
	uniformTime: boolean,
	maxDt: number
): number
	local minStepDt = ProjectileMotion.MinStepDt
	local availableDt = remaining * chunkScale
	if availableDt <= minStepDt then
		return 0
	end

	local predictedVelocity = velocity + accelerationVector * availableDt
	local movementVelocity = (velocity + predictedVelocity) * 0.5
	local speed = movementVelocity.Magnitude
	local stepDt = math.min(availableDt, lifeRemaining, maxDt)
	if speed > 1e-5 then
		stepDt = math.min(stepDt, ProjectileMotion.GetAdaptiveMaxDistance(speed, nearEntities) / speed)
		if not uniformTime then
			stepDt = math.min(
				stepDt,
				ProjectileMotion.GetTimeScaleBoundaryDt(
					position,
					movementVelocity,
					ChunkManager.ChunkSize,
					ChunkManager.UseY,
					chunkScale,
					stepDt,
					Planner.ChunkTimeScaleAt
				),
				ChunkManager.GetRadialTimeScaleBoundaryDt(position, movementVelocity, stepDt)
			)
		end
	end
	stepDt = math.min(
		stepDt,
		ProjectileMotion.GetCurvatureStepDt(velocity, accelerationVector, ProjectileMotion.CurveError)
	)

	-- Boundary and curvature limits can shrink a step toward zero -- e.g. a
	-- projectile resting a hair before a chunk plane. Floor it so they can
	-- never stall progress; overshooting a boundary by minStepDt of travel
	-- is far below anything visible.
	return math.max(stepDt, math.min(minStepDt, availableDt, lifeRemaining))
end

return Planner
-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/shared/ProjectileStepPlanner.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/shared/ProjectileProtocol.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!strict
--[[
	ProjectileProtocol.luau
	The wire format between the server projectile system
	(ServerScriptService.Server.Projectile/Replication.luau, sending) and
	ProjectileClient (receiving). Channel names and payload shapes live here
	so both sides are type-checked against one definition.

	Beam snapshots carry a synchronized real-time epoch and global scale.
	Clients shift each packet's epoch by its spawn transit time (so it starts
	at the received pose, like other projectiles), predict endpoints together
	and tessellate locally. Topology/clipping and hits remain server-authoritative. Ordinary
	projectile snapshots retain their existing receipt-time baseline.
]]

local Protocol = {}

Protocol.Channels = {
	SpawnBatch = "ProjSpawnBatch", -- { SpawnPayload }
	Move = "ProjMove", -- { MovePayload }
	HitBatch = "ProjHitBatch", -- { HitPayload }
	RangeExit = "ProjRangeExit", -- { number }; not projectile death
	Sync = "ProjSync", -- SyncPayload
	TimeScale = "ProjTimeScale", -- TimeScalePayload
	Ray = "ProjRay", -- RayPayload
}

export type Acceleration = number | Vector3

export type VisualSpec = {
	Shape: string?,
	Size: Vector3?,
	Color: Color3?,
	Style: string?,
	Core: Color3?,
}

-- Optional fields are omitted when equal to the client default (noted),
-- because remote events serialize every key name per entry.
export type SpawnPayload = {
	Id: number,
	Position: Vector3,
	Velocity: Vector3,
	Lifetime: number, -- dilated seconds remaining
	MaxRealLifetime: number, -- real seconds remaining
	AccelerationDirection: Vector3?,
	Model: Instance?,
	Visual: VisualSpec?,
	Gravity: Acceleration?, -- 0
	Acceleration: Acceleration?, -- 0
	MinSpeed: number?, -- 0
	MaxSpeed: number?, -- math.huge
	Synced: boolean?, -- false
	TimeScale: number?, -- 1
	VisualScale: number?, -- 1
	ServerTime: number?, -- synchronized real-time epoch for predicted beams
	GlobalScale: number?,
	Beam: { Length: number, Radius: number, Origin: Vector3, ChannelId: number?, PreviousId: number?,
		Path: { Vector3 }?, Clipped: boolean? }?, -- linked stream centerline
	DestroyDelay: number?, -- 0
	WaitForParticles: boolean?, -- true
	WaitForTrails: boolean?, -- true
	ActivateParticlesOnCreate: boolean?, -- false
}

-- Either a homing pose (Bounced nil) or a one-shot bounce snap.
export type MovePayload = {
	Id: number,
	Position: Vector3,
	Velocity: Vector3,
	Bounced: boolean?,
	Corrected: boolean?, -- authoritative beam-body contact, not a ricochet flash
	BeamPreviousId: number?, -- 0 explicitly unlinks; nil means not a beam
	ServerTime: number?,
	GlobalScale: number?,
	TimeScale: number?,
	BeamPath: { Vector3 }?, -- authoritative linked body, clipped at obstructions
	BeamClipped: boolean?, -- true only when the body stops before its PreviousId
	Lifetime: number?,
	Point: Vector3?, -- bounce contact point
	Normal: Vector3?, -- bounce surface normal
}

export type HitPayload = {
	Id: number,
	Position: Vector3,
	Normal: Vector3,
	Kind: string?, -- nil: expired without hitting anything
	BeamBody: boolean?,
	BeamPath: { Vector3 }?,
	BeamClipped: boolean?,
}

export type SyncPayload = {
	Id: number,
	Synced: boolean,
	Position: Vector3,
	Velocity: Vector3,
}

export type TimeScalePayload = {
	Id: number,
	TimeScale: number,
}

export type RayPayload = {
	From: Vector3,
	To: Vector3,
	LowRes: boolean,
}

return Protocol
-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/shared/ProjectileProtocol.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/shared/ProjectileCodec.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!strict
--!native
--!optimize 2
--[[
	ProjectileCodec.luau
	Binary wire format for the two per-frame projectile batches, ProjMove and
	ProjHitBatch (see ProjectileProtocol for the payload fields). A table batch
	makes Roblox send every key name of every entry; these are packed buffers
	instead: each entry is a fixed header plus only the optional fields it
	has, flagged in a bitmask.

	The server encodes each entry ONCE (EncodeMove / EncodeHit -> buffer) and
	Join()s the chunks for each recipient, so nearby players sharing shots
	don't re-encode them. The client decodes a whole message back into the
	same payload tables (DecodeMoves / DecodeHits), so its handlers don't
	change.

	Vectors are 3 x f32 (positions keep ~1/1000 stud at 8000 studs out);
	ServerTime stays f64 -- beam epochs need its full precision.

	Move entry:  u32 Id, u16 flags, f32x3 Position, f32x3 Velocity, then by flag:
	             u32 BeamPreviousId, f64 ServerTime, f32 GlobalScale,
	             f32 TimeScale, path BeamPath, f32 Lifetime, f32x3 Point,
	             f32x3 Normal          (Bounced / Corrected / BeamClipped are flags)
	Hit entry:   u32 Id, u8 flags, f32x3 Position, f32x3 Normal, then by flag:
	             string Kind, path BeamPath        (BeamBody / BeamClipped are flags)
	path:        u16 count, count x f32x3;  string: u8 length, bytes
]]

local ProjectileCodec = {}

local MOVE_BOUNCED = 0x001
local MOVE_CORRECTED = 0x002
local MOVE_PREVIOUS = 0x004
local MOVE_SERVER_TIME = 0x008
local MOVE_GLOBAL_SCALE = 0x010
local MOVE_TIME_SCALE = 0x020
local MOVE_PATH = 0x040
local MOVE_CLIPPED = 0x080
local MOVE_LIFETIME = 0x100
local MOVE_POINT = 0x200
local MOVE_NORMAL = 0x400

local HIT_KIND = 0x01
local HIT_BEAM_BODY = 0x02
local HIT_PATH = 0x04
local HIT_CLIPPED = 0x08

local MAX_PATH = 65535
local MAX_KIND = 255

local writeu8, writeu16, writeu32 = buffer.writeu8, buffer.writeu16, buffer.writeu32
local writef32, writef64, writestring = buffer.writef32, buffer.writef64, buffer.writestring
local readu8, readu16, readu32 = buffer.readu8, buffer.readu16, buffer.readu32
local readf32, readf64, readstring = buffer.readf32, buffer.readf64, buffer.readstring
local band, bor = bit32.band, bit32.bor

local function writeVector(b: buffer, offset: number, v: Vector3): number
	writef32(b, offset, v.X)
	writef32(b, offset + 4, v.Y)
	writef32(b, offset + 8, v.Z)
	return offset + 12
end

local function readVector(b: buffer, offset: number): (Vector3, number)
	return Vector3.new(readf32(b, offset), readf32(b, offset + 4), readf32(b, offset + 8)), offset + 12
end

local function pathSize(path: { Vector3 }): number
	return 2 + math.min(#path, MAX_PATH) * 12
end

local function writePath(b: buffer, offset: number, path: { Vector3 }): number
	local count = math.min(#path, MAX_PATH)
	writeu16(b, offset, count)
	offset += 2
	for index = 1, count do
		offset = writeVector(b, offset, path[index])
	end
	return offset
end

local function readPath(b: buffer, offset: number): ({ Vector3 }, number)
	local count = readu16(b, offset)
	offset += 2
	local path = table.create(count)
	for index = 1, count do
		path[index], offset = readVector(b, offset)
	end
	return path, offset
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- ProjMove
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

function ProjectileCodec.EncodeMove(p: any): buffer
	local flags, size = 0, 4 + 2 + 12 + 12
	if p.Bounced then flags = bor(flags, MOVE_BOUNCED) end
	if p.Corrected then flags = bor(flags, MOVE_CORRECTED) end
	if p.BeamPreviousId ~= nil then flags = bor(flags, MOVE_PREVIOUS); size += 4 end
	if p.ServerTime ~= nil then flags = bor(flags, MOVE_SERVER_TIME); size += 8 end
	if p.GlobalScale ~= nil then flags = bor(flags, MOVE_GLOBAL_SCALE); size += 4 end
	if p.TimeScale ~= nil then flags = bor(flags, MOVE_TIME_SCALE); size += 4 end
	if p.BeamPath ~= nil then flags = bor(flags, MOVE_PATH); size += pathSize(p.BeamPath) end
	if p.BeamClipped then flags = bor(flags, MOVE_CLIPPED) end
	if p.Lifetime ~= nil then flags = bor(flags, MOVE_LIFETIME); size += 4 end
	if p.Point ~= nil then flags = bor(flags, MOVE_POINT); size += 12 end
	if p.Normal ~= nil then flags = bor(flags, MOVE_NORMAL); size += 12 end

	local b = buffer.create(size)
	writeu32(b, 0, p.Id)
	writeu16(b, 4, flags)
	local offset = writeVector(b, 6, p.Position)
	offset = writeVector(b, offset, p.Velocity)
	if p.BeamPreviousId ~= nil then writeu32(b, offset, p.BeamPreviousId); offset += 4 end
	if p.ServerTime ~= nil then writef64(b, offset, p.ServerTime); offset += 8 end
	if p.GlobalScale ~= nil then writef32(b, offset, p.GlobalScale); offset += 4 end
	if p.TimeScale ~= nil then writef32(b, offset, p.TimeScale); offset += 4 end
	if p.BeamPath ~= nil then offset = writePath(b, offset, p.BeamPath) end
	if p.Lifetime ~= nil then writef32(b, offset, p.Lifetime); offset += 4 end
	if p.Point ~= nil then offset = writeVector(b, offset, p.Point) end
	if p.Normal ~= nil then writeVector(b, offset, p.Normal) end
	return b
end

function ProjectileCodec.DecodeMoves(b: buffer): { any }
	local list = {}
	local offset, length = 0, buffer.len(b)
	while offset < length do
		local p: any = { Id = readu32(b, offset) }
		local flags = readu16(b, offset + 4)
		p.Position, offset = readVector(b, offset + 6)
		p.Velocity, offset = readVector(b, offset)
		if band(flags, MOVE_BOUNCED) ~= 0 then p.Bounced = true end
		if band(flags, MOVE_CORRECTED) ~= 0 then p.Corrected = true end
		if band(flags, MOVE_PREVIOUS) ~= 0 then p.BeamPreviousId = readu32(b, offset); offset += 4 end
		if band(flags, MOVE_SERVER_TIME) ~= 0 then p.ServerTime = readf64(b, offset); offset += 8 end
		if band(flags, MOVE_GLOBAL_SCALE) ~= 0 then p.GlobalScale = readf32(b, offset); offset += 4 end
		if band(flags, MOVE_TIME_SCALE) ~= 0 then p.TimeScale = readf32(b, offset); offset += 4 end
		if band(flags, MOVE_PATH) ~= 0 then p.BeamPath, offset = readPath(b, offset) end
		if band(flags, MOVE_CLIPPED) ~= 0 then p.BeamClipped = true end
		if band(flags, MOVE_LIFETIME) ~= 0 then p.Lifetime = readf32(b, offset); offset += 4 end
		if band(flags, MOVE_POINT) ~= 0 then p.Point, offset = readVector(b, offset) end
		if band(flags, MOVE_NORMAL) ~= 0 then p.Normal, offset = readVector(b, offset) end
		table.insert(list, p)
	end
	return list
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- ProjHitBatch
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

function ProjectileCodec.EncodeHit(p: any): buffer
	local flags, size = 0, 4 + 1 + 12 + 12
	local kind: string? = p.Kind
	if kind ~= nil then
		kind = string.sub(kind, 1, MAX_KIND)
		flags = bor(flags, HIT_KIND)
		size += 1 + #(kind :: string)
	end
	if p.BeamBody then flags = bor(flags, HIT_BEAM_BODY) end
	if p.BeamPath ~= nil then flags = bor(flags, HIT_PATH); size += pathSize(p.BeamPath) end
	if p.BeamClipped then flags = bor(flags, HIT_CLIPPED) end

	local b = buffer.create(size)
	writeu32(b, 0, p.Id)
	writeu8(b, 4, flags)
	local offset = writeVector(b, 5, p.Position)
	offset = writeVector(b, offset, p.Normal)
	if kind ~= nil then
		writeu8(b, offset, #kind)
		writestring(b, offset + 1, kind)
		offset += 1 + #kind
	end
	if p.BeamPath ~= nil then writePath(b, offset, p.BeamPath) end
	return b
end

function ProjectileCodec.DecodeHits(b: buffer): { any }
	local list = {}
	local offset, length = 0, buffer.len(b)
	while offset < length do
		local p: any = { Id = readu32(b, offset) }
		local flags = readu8(b, offset + 4)
		p.Position, offset = readVector(b, offset + 5)
		p.Normal, offset = readVector(b, offset)
		if band(flags, HIT_KIND) ~= 0 then
			local count = readu8(b, offset)
			p.Kind = readstring(b, offset + 1, count)
			offset += 1 + count
		end
		if band(flags, HIT_BEAM_BODY) ~= 0 then p.BeamBody = true end
		if band(flags, HIT_PATH) ~= 0 then p.BeamPath, offset = readPath(b, offset) end
		if band(flags, HIT_CLIPPED) ~= 0 then p.BeamClipped = true end
		table.insert(list, p)
	end
	return list
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Batching
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Concatenates encoded entries into one message.
function ProjectileCodec.Join(chunks: { buffer }): buffer
	local total = 0
	for _, chunk in chunks do
		total += buffer.len(chunk)
	end
	local out = buffer.create(total)
	local offset = 0
	for _, chunk in chunks do
		local size = buffer.len(chunk)
		buffer.copy(out, offset, chunk, 0, size)
		offset += size
	end
	return out
end

return ProjectileCodec
-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/shared/ProjectileCodec.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/shared/Projectile/BeamPath.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!strict
-- Shared *physical* centerline of a continuous stream. A newer sample is the
-- back of its section; the preceding sample is its front. Turning the input
-- therefore bends the stream instead of emitting unrelated parallel bars.
-- Shared projectile geometry: both server collision and client cylinders use
-- these exact endpoints. Kept replicated because the client needs the same math.
local BeamPath = {}
BeamPath.MaxStretch = 32
BeamPath.MaxJoinersPerLink = 32

export type Joiner = { Position: Vector3 }

-- Plan against the real bounce corners, never a shortcut through a wall.
-- Count before allocating joiners so a huge flick is rejected in bounded work.
function BeamPath.Plan(back: Vector3, front: Vector3, backTurns: { Vector3 }?, frontTurns: { Vector3 }?): ({ Vector3 }?, number)
	local behind, ahead = backTurns or {}, frontTurns or {}
	if #behind > #ahead then return nil, 0 end
	local corners = { back }
	local count = 0
	local function append(point: Vector3): boolean
		local distance = (point - corners[#corners]).Magnitude
		if distance <= 1e-4 then return true end
		count += math.max(math.ceil(distance / BeamPath.MaxStretch) - 1, 0)
		if count > BeamPath.MaxJoinersPerLink then return false end
		table.insert(corners, point)
		return true
	end
	for index = #behind + 1, #ahead do
		if not append(ahead[index]) then return nil, count end
	end
	if not append(front) then return nil, count end
	return corners, count
end

-- Pool only lightweight control points: no projectile, Instance, damage
-- handler or thread per joiner. Retained pool entries are reused after shrink.
function BeamPath.Fill(corners: { Vector3 }, pool: { Joiner }?, output: { Vector3 }?, cornerIndices: { number }?): { Vector3 }
	local points = output or {}
	table.clear(points)
	if cornerIndices then table.clear(cornerIndices); table.insert(cornerIndices, 1) end
	table.insert(points, corners[1])
	local used = 0
	for index = 1, #corners - 1 do
		local a, b = corners[index], corners[index + 1]
		local pieces = math.max(1, math.ceil((b - a).Magnitude / BeamPath.MaxStretch))
		for piece = 1, pieces - 1 do
			local position = a:Lerp(b, piece / pieces)
			used += 1
			if pool then
				local joiner = pool[used]
				if not joiner then joiner = { Position = position }; pool[used] = joiner
				else joiner.Position = position end
			end
			table.insert(points, position)
		end
		table.insert(points, b)
		if cornerIndices then table.insert(cornerIndices, #points) end
	end
	return points
end

-- Joiners are deterministic collinear subdivisions. Send only real corners
-- and the clipped endpoint, not a larger network payload for every joiner.
-- The index map preserves exact bends without approximate angle tests.
function BeamPath.Compact(points: { Vector3 }, cornerIndices: { number }?): { Vector3 }
	if not cornerIndices or #points <= 2 then return points end
	local result = { points[1] }
	for index = 2, #cornerIndices do
		local at = cornerIndices[index]
		if at >= #points then break end
		table.insert(result, points[at])
	end
	if (points[#points] - result[#result]).Magnitude > 1e-4 then table.insert(result, points[#points]) end
	return result
end

function BeamPath.Connect(back: Vector3, front: Vector3, backTurns: { Vector3 }?, frontTurns: { Vector3 }?): { Vector3 }?
	local corners = BeamPath.Plan(back, front, backTurns, frontTurns)
	return if corners then BeamPath.Fill(corners) else nil
end

return BeamPath
-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/shared/Projectile/BeamPath.luau
-- =============================================================================

	behaviour. Entity.luau and Signal.luau are not strictly typed, so the
	parts of them this system relies on are described structurally here.

local Shared = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("Shared")

	Instance: Instance?,
	TimeScale: number?,
	IsDestroyed: boolean,
	Health: number,
	HeadRadius: number,
	HitboxRadius: number,

}

-- A world contact: a RaycastResult converted to a plain table, or a
-- synthetic contact (lag-compensated hit, bounce, expiry).

	Normal: Vector3,

-- Payload of projectile.OnHit -- see the "Events" section in init.luau.

	TargetTags: { string }?,
	AcquireRadius: number?,
	Retarget: boolean,
	ReacquireRate: number,
	AcquireInterval: number,
	Permalock: boolean,
	TurnRate: number,
	Delay: number,
}

-- Caller-facing Projectile.new config -- see the module doc comment in
-- init.luau for what each field means. Every value is treated as untrusted
-- and normalized by Config.normalize before use.
export type Config = {
	Origin: Vector3?,
	Direction: Vector3?,
	TargetPosition: Vector3?,
	Speed: number?,
	Acceleration: Acceleration?,
	AccelerationDirection: Vector3?,
	MinSpeed: number?,
	MaxSpeed: number?,
	Lifetime: number?,
	MaxRealLifetime: number?,
	TimeScale: number?,
	Damage: number?,
	Source: EntityLike?,
	-- `{ any }` rather than `{ Instance }`: table types are invariant, so a
	-- caller's `{ Model }` would not type-check. Non-Instances are dropped
	-- by Config.normalize.
	IgnoreInstances: { any }?,
	Filter: ((entity: EntityLike) -> boolean)?,
	Gravity: Acceleration?,
	Radius: number?,
	Bounces: number?,
	Restitution: number?,
	Penetration: number?,
	MaxPierces: number?,

	DestroyDelay: number?,
	WaitForParticles: boolean?,
	WaitForTrails: boolean?,
	ActivateParticlesOnCreate: boolean?,
	OnBounce: ((projectile: any, contact: Contact) -> ())?,
	RewindSeconds: number?,
	Spread: number?, -- Projectile.Burst only
}

-- Live projectile state. Public (PascalCase) fields are readable and
-- writable by abilities; underscore fields are internal bookkeeping.
export type State = {
	Id: number,
	Position: Vector3,
	Velocity: Vector3,
	Speed: number,
	Acceleration: Acceleration,
	AccelerationDirection: Vector3?,

	MaxSpeed: number,

	Restitution: number,
	Penetration: number,
	PiercesLeft: number,
	PierceFalloff: number,

	Homing: Homing?,
	HomingDelay: number,
	HomingTarget: HomingTarget?,

	VisualRange: number,
	Model: Instance?,
	Visual: VisualSpec?,
	VisualScale: number,
	Beam: { Length: number, ChannelId: number?, PreviousId: number? }?,
	DestroyDelay: number,

	WaitForTrails: boolean,
	ActivateParticlesOnCreate: boolean,

	OnDestroy: Signal<DestroyInfo>,

	RewindSeconds: number,
	Dead: boolean,

	_spawnRealTime: number,
	_acquireTimer: number,
	_ignore: { [EntityLike]: boolean },
	_rewindTime: number,
	_rewindCache: { [EntityLike]: { Body: Vector3, Head: Vector3? } },
	_simulationDebt: number,
	_rayParams: RaycastParams,
	-- beam body casts: _rayParams plus pierced entities, rebuilt only when the
	-- pierced count changes (see ResolveBeamSpan); never mutated, so beam
	-- samples cloned from this packet may share it
	_spanParams: RaycastParams?,
	_spanPierced: number?,
	-- parallel movement (Parallel.luau): its raycast filter's id, queued /
	-- slotted, and the frame mark of a result applied before this frame's step
	-- loop (+mark: alive, -mark: dead)
	_filterId: number?,
	_slot: number?, -- its Store record while live (see Store.luau)
	_parallelState: number?,
	_sweepMark: number?,
	_spawnStreamed: boolean,
	_streamedSynced: boolean,
	_lastStreamedTimeScale: number,
	_beamOrigin: Vector3?,
	_beamTurns: { Vector3 }?,
	_beamPrevious: any?,
	_beamBodyHit: boolean?,
	_beamSpan: { Vector3 }?,
	_beamSpanClipped: boolean?,
	_beamJoiner: boolean?, -- independently simulated/colliding subdivision
	_beamJoinerWorldStop: boolean?,
	_beamReserveChildren: ((number) -> boolean)?,
	_beamBindChild: ((any, number) -> ())?,
	_beamScaleEnergy: ((number) -> ())?,
}

-- What a hit resolver decided:
--  "pass"        keeps flying on the same trajectory (pierce, penetration,
--                or nudging past an ignored/rewound-away entity)
--  "bounce"      reflected; the client is re-baselined by a bounce snap
--  "destroy"     the caller must Destroy() with the returned kind
--  "fallthrough" entity filtered out; resolve as world geometry instead
export type Verdict = "pass" | "bounce" | "destroy" | "fallthrough"

-- ModuleScripts must return exactly one non-nil value.
return {}

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/Config.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!strict
--[[
	Projectile/Config.luau
	Turns a caller's Projectile.new config into validated settings. Every
	value is treated as untrusted -- configs are assembled from weapon data,
	spell graphs and (in Studio) a client-tunable debug panel -- so NaN,
	+-inf, wrong types and out-of-range numbers are all normalized here, once,
	and nothing downstream has to re-check them.

	Numbers clamp to SafeMath.Limit (1e9) instead of being rejected, so an
	absurd value still behaves predictably; NaN falls back to the default.
]]

local Shared = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("Shared")
local SafeMath = require(Shared:WaitForChild("SafeMath"))

local Types = require(script.Parent.Types)

local Config = {}

local DEFAULT_SPEED = 100
local DEFAULT_LIFETIME = 5
local DEFAULT_RESTITUTION = 0.5
local DEFAULT_TURN_RATE = math.rad(120)
local DEFAULT_REACQUIRE_RATE = 0.3
-- Dilated seconds between searches while no target is held; see Homing.
local DEFAULT_ACQUIRE_INTERVAL = 0.1

export type Settings = {
	Origin: Vector3,
	Direction: Vector3,
	Speed: number,
	Acceleration: Types.Acceleration,
	AccelerationDirection: Vector3?,
	MinSpeed: number,
	MaxSpeed: number,
	Gravity: Types.Acceleration,
	Radius: number,
	Lifetime: number,
	MaxRealLifetime: number,
	TimeScale: number,
	Damage: number,
	Source: Types.EntityLike?,
	IgnoreInstances: { Instance }?,
	Filter: ((entity: Types.EntityLike) -> boolean)?,
	Bounces: number,
	Restitution: number,
	Penetration: number,
	MaxPierces: number,
	PierceFalloff: number,
	Homing: Types.Homing?,
	Visualize: boolean,
	VisualRange: number,
	Model: Instance?,
	Visual: Types.VisualSpec?,
	VisualScale: number,
	Beam: { Length: number, ChannelId: number?, PreviousId: number? }?,
	DestroyDelay: number,
	WaitForParticles: boolean,
	WaitForTrails: boolean,
	ActivateParticlesOnCreate: boolean,
	OnBounce: ((projectile: any, contact: Types.Contact) -> ())?,
	RewindSeconds: number,
}

local function acceleration(value: unknown): Types.Acceleration
	if typeof(value) == "Vector3" then
		return SafeMath.vector(value, Vector3.zero)
	end
	return SafeMath.number(value, 0)
end

local function count(value: unknown): number
	return math.floor(SafeMath.number(value, 0, 0))
end

local function optionalDirection(value: unknown): Vector3?
	if typeof(value) ~= "Vector3" then
		return nil
	end
	local direction = SafeMath.unit(value, Vector3.zero)
	return if direction == Vector3.zero then nil else direction
end

-- Keeps only real Instances; anything else in the list is dropped.
local function instanceList(value: unknown): { Instance }?
	if typeof(value) ~= "table" then
		return nil
	end
	local list: { Instance } = {}
	for _, item in value :: { any } do
		if typeof(item) == "Instance" then
			table.insert(list, item)
		end
	end
	return list
end

local function optionalFunction<T>(value: T?): T?
	return if typeof(value) == "function" then value else nil
end

-- The launch direction: toward TargetPosition when given, else Direction.
-- Degenerate aims (zero, NaN) fall back to +Z rather than producing NaN.
function Config.direction(raw: Types.Config, origin: Vector3): Vector3
	if typeof(raw.TargetPosition) == "Vector3" then
		local target = SafeMath.vector(raw.TargetPosition, origin)
		return SafeMath.direction(target - origin, Vector3.zAxis)
	end
	return SafeMath.unit(raw.Direction, Vector3.zAxis)
end

function Config.normalizeHoming(raw: Types.HomingOptions?): Types.Homing?
	if typeof(raw) ~= "table" then
		return nil
	end
	local target = raw.Target
	if typeof(target) == "Vector3" then
		target = SafeMath.vector(target, Vector3.zero)
	end
	local acquireRadius = raw.AcquireRadius
	return {
		Target = target,
		TargetTag = if typeof(raw.TargetTag) == "string" then raw.TargetTag else nil,
		TargetTags = if typeof(raw.TargetTags) == "table" then raw.TargetTags else nil,
		-- nil keeps its meaning of "unbounded"; NaN is treated as unset.
		AcquireRadius = if typeof(acquireRadius) == "number" and acquireRadius == acquireRadius
			then SafeMath.number(acquireRadius, 0, 0)
			else nil,
		Retarget = raw.Retarget == true,
		ReacquireRate = SafeMath.number(raw.ReacquireRate, DEFAULT_REACQUIRE_RATE, 0),
		AcquireInterval = SafeMath.number(raw.AcquireInterval, DEFAULT_ACQUIRE_INTERVAL, 0),
		Permalock = raw.Permalock == true,
		TurnRate = SafeMath.number(raw.TurnRate, DEFAULT_TURN_RATE, 0),
		Delay = SafeMath.number(raw.Delay, 0, 0),
	}
end

function Config.normalize(raw: Types.Config, defaultMaxRealLifetime: number): Settings
	local origin = SafeMath.vector(raw.Origin, Vector3.zero)
	local minSpeed = SafeMath.number(raw.MinSpeed, 0, 0)
	local visual = raw.Visual
	local model = raw.Model
	return {
		Origin = origin,
		Direction = Config.direction(raw, origin),
		Speed = SafeMath.number(raw.Speed, if typeof(raw.Beam) == "table" then 2000 else DEFAULT_SPEED, 0),
		Acceleration = acceleration(raw.Acceleration),
		AccelerationDirection = optionalDirection(raw.AccelerationDirection),
		MinSpeed = minSpeed,
		-- math.huge stays the "no cap" sentinel; a cap below MinSpeed is raised to it.
		MaxSpeed = SafeMath.cap(raw.MaxSpeed, minSpeed),
		Gravity = acceleration(raw.Gravity),
		Radius = SafeMath.number(raw.Radius, if typeof(raw.Beam) == "table" then 0.35 else 0, 0),
		Lifetime = SafeMath.number(raw.Lifetime, if typeof(raw.Beam) == "table" then 3 else DEFAULT_LIFETIME, 0),
		MaxRealLifetime = SafeMath.number(raw.MaxRealLifetime, defaultMaxRealLifetime, 0),
		TimeScale = SafeMath.number(raw.TimeScale, 1, 0),
		Damage = SafeMath.number(raw.Damage, 0),
		Source = if typeof(raw.Source) == "table" then raw.Source else nil,
		IgnoreInstances = instanceList(raw.IgnoreInstances),
		Filter = optionalFunction(raw.Filter),
		Bounces = count(raw.Bounces),
		Restitution = SafeMath.number(raw.Restitution, DEFAULT_RESTITUTION, 0),
		Penetration = SafeMath.number(raw.Penetration, 0, 0),
		MaxPierces = count(raw.MaxPierces),
		PierceFalloff = SafeMath.number(raw.PierceFalloff, 0, 0, 1),
		Homing = Config.normalizeHoming(raw.Homing),
		Visualize = raw.Visualize == true,
		VisualRange = SafeMath.cap(raw.VisualRange, 0),
		Model = if typeof(model) == "Instance" then model else nil,
		Visual = if typeof(visual) == "table" then visual else nil,
		VisualScale = SafeMath.number(raw.VisualScale, 1, 0.05, 20),
		Beam = if typeof(raw.Beam) == "table" then {
			Length = SafeMath.number(raw.Beam.Length, 24, 0.05, 512),
			ChannelId = if typeof(raw.Beam.ChannelId) == "number" then math.floor(SafeMath.number(raw.Beam.ChannelId, 1, 1)) else nil,
			PreviousId = if typeof(raw.Beam.PreviousId) == "number" then math.floor(SafeMath.number(raw.Beam.PreviousId, 1, 1)) else nil,
		} else nil,
		DestroyDelay = SafeMath.number(raw.DestroyDelay, 0, 0),
		WaitForParticles = raw.WaitForParticles ~= false,
		WaitForTrails = raw.WaitForTrails ~= false,
		ActivateParticlesOnCreate = raw.ActivateParticlesOnCreate == true,
		OnBounce = optionalFunction(raw.OnBounce),
		RewindSeconds = SafeMath.number(raw.RewindSeconds, 0, 0),
	}
end

-- Burst cone half-angle in degrees.
function Config.spread(raw: Types.Config): number
	return SafeMath.number(raw.Spread, 0, 0, 180)
end

return Config
-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/server/Projectile/Config.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/Math.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!native
--!strict
--!optimize 2
--[[
	Projectile/Math.luau
	Pure geometry helpers shared by the other Projectile server modules
	(Homing, RewindHit, init). No projectile/entity state, no side effects.
	Finite-number guards live in Shared.SafeMath.
]]

local Shared = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("Shared")
local SafeMath = require(Shared:WaitForChild("SafeMath"))

local Math = {}

-- Rotate `from` toward `to` by at most `maxAngle` radians; returns a unit vector.
function Math.rotateTowards(from: Vector3, to: Vector3, maxAngle: number): Vector3
	local fromDir = SafeMath.direction(from, Vector3.zAxis)
	local toDir = SafeMath.direction(to, fromDir)
	local dot = math.clamp(fromDir:Dot(toDir), -1, 1)
	local angle = math.acos(dot)
	if angle <= maxAngle or angle < 1e-4 then
		return toDir
	end
	local axis = fromDir:Cross(toDir)
	if axis.Magnitude < 1e-4 then
		-- opposite directions: pick an arbitrary perpendicular axis
		axis = if math.abs(fromDir.Y) < 0.99 then fromDir:Cross(Vector3.yAxis) else fromDir:Cross(Vector3.xAxis)
	end
	return CFrame.fromAxisAngle(axis.Unit, maxAngle):VectorToWorldSpace(fromDir)
end

-- Closest point on segment [a,b] to point p, and the distance to it. Used by
-- lag-compensated hit detection to test a rewound entity position against a
-- substep's movement segment.
function Math.closestPointOnSegment(p: Vector3, a: Vector3, b: Vector3): (Vector3, number)
	local ab = b - a
	local lengthSq = ab:Dot(ab)
	local t = if lengthSq > 1e-8 then math.clamp((p - a):Dot(ab) / lengthSq, 0, 1) else 0
	local closest = a + ab * t
	return closest, (p - closest).Magnitude
end

-- How far along the chord from `from` to `from + displacement` the point
-- lies, as a 0..1 fraction (0 for a degenerate chord).
function Math.chordFraction(from: Vector3, displacement: Vector3, point: Vector3): number
	local lengthSq = displacement:Dot(displacement)
	if not (lengthSq >= 1e-10) then
		return 0
	end
	return math.clamp((point - from):Dot(displacement) / lengthSq, 0, 1)
end

-- Uniformly random direction within `spreadDeg` of the unit vector `dir`.
function Math.coneDirection(dir: Vector3, spreadDeg: number): Vector3
	if not (spreadDeg > 0) then
		return dir
	end
	local spread = math.rad(math.min(spreadDeg, 180))
	-- sqrt for an even areal distribution across the cone
	local theta = math.sqrt(math.random()) * spread
	local roll = math.random() * 2 * math.pi
	local up = if math.abs(dir.Y) < 0.99 then Vector3.yAxis else Vector3.xAxis
	local right = dir:Cross(up).Unit
	local realUp = right:Cross(dir).Unit
	-- Rotate rather than offset by tan(theta): tan blows up toward 90 degrees.
	local radial = right * math.cos(roll) + realUp * math.sin(roll)
	return SafeMath.direction(dir * math.cos(theta) + radial * math.sin(theta), dir)
end

return Math
-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/server/Projectile/Math.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/Raycast.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!native
--!strict
--!optimize 2
--[[
	Projectile/Raycast.luau
	Physical ray/capsule movement casts, world/entity hit resolution, and wall
	penetration. The resolvers decide what a contact does and apply its
	immediate effects (OnHit, pierce bookkeeping, reflection, nudging past the
	surface), then return a Types.Verdict; lifecycle -- Destroy(), time
	accounting -- stays with the caller in init.luau.
]]

local Shared = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("Shared")
local Entity = require(Shared:WaitForChild("Entity"))
local ChunkManager = require(Shared:WaitForChild("ChunkManager"))
local SafeMath = require(Shared:WaitForChild("SafeMath"))

local Replication = require(script.Parent.Replication)
local Occupancy = require(script.Parent.Occupancy)
local Types = require(script.Parent.Types)

type State = Types.State
type Verdict = Types.Verdict

local Raycast = {}

-- Clearance when stepping just past a surface after a pass-through contact.
local PASS_CLEARANCE = 0.1
-- Clearance off a surface after a bounce.
local BOUNCE_CLEARANCE = 0.05

-- Built once per projectile and cached on it (Source never changes after
-- construction), reused for every raycast that projectile makes -- Roblox
-- re-evaluates FilterDescendantsInstances against the live scene at cast time, so
-- one instance is safe to reuse across many casts/frames; this only removes the
-- allocation churn of rebuilding it every substep, not a correctness change.
-- NOTE: if a future feature needs to grow the exclude list dynamically (e.g.
-- adding pierced entities instead of the current position-nudge approach),
-- mutating `ignore` in place won't take effect -- FilterDescendantsInstances
-- would need reassigning.
-- Shared params by content: nothing writes to a projectile's _rayParams, so
-- every projectile ignoring the same instances (a burst, a stress test, one
-- player's shots) uses one RaycastParams instead of building its own. Keyed
-- by a trie of the ignored instances; reset when it grows past
-- MAX_SHARED_PARAMS (dead characters), which only costs a rebuild.
local MAX_SHARED_PARAMS = 1024
local sharedParams: { [any]: any } = {}
local sharedCount = 0
local LEAF = newproxy() -- (trie key for a node's params; can't collide with an Instance)

function Raycast.buildRayParams(source: Types.EntityLike?, ignoreInstances: { Instance }?): RaycastParams
	local ignore: { Instance } = {}
	local sourceInstance = source and source.Instance
	if sourceInstance then
		table.insert(ignore, sourceInstance)
	end
	-- Excluded independently of Source: Source only exists once the firing
	-- entity is registered with the Entity system (see PlayerManager.server.luau),
	-- so a shot fired in the window before that registration lands would
	-- otherwise have nothing excluding the shooter's own character from this
	-- raycast -- IgnoreInstances closes that gap without depending on timing.
	if ignoreInstances then
		table.move(ignoreInstances, 1, #ignoreInstances, #ignore + 1, ignore)
	end
	local node = sharedParams
	for _, instance in ignore do
		local nextNode = node[instance]
		if not nextNode then
			nextNode = {}
			node[instance] = nextNode
		end
		node = nextNode
	end
	local shared = node[LEAF]
	if shared then
		return shared
	end
	local params = RaycastParams.new()
	params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
	params.FilterDescendantsInstances = ignore
	params.IgnoreWater = true
	sharedCount += 1
	if sharedCount > MAX_SHARED_PARAMS then
		table.clear(sharedParams)
		sharedCount = 0
		return params
	end
	node[LEAF] = params
	return params
end

-- Sweeps the projectile's body along `displacement`. Returns the contact as a
-- plain table (see Types.Contact) or nil. Distance is how far the ray -- or
-- the sphere's center -- travelled, which is what the time accounting in
-- init.luau needs; for a Spherecast, Position is the surface point instead.
function Raycast.castMovement(projectile: State, origin: Vector3, displacement: Vector3, overrideParams: RaycastParams?): Types.Contact?
	-- Provably empty space: the cast would find nothing, so don't make it
	-- (see Occupancy -- it only says yes when nothing could be in the way).
	if Occupancy.SegmentClear(origin, displacement, projectile.Radius) then
		return nil
	end
	local params = overrideParams or projectile._rayParams
	local result
	if projectile.Radius > 0 then
		-- Sweeping a sphere along a line is exactly a capsule: a cylindrical
		-- body of Radius around this segment plus spherical caps at both ends.
		-- Adjacent adaptive substeps share the cap at their common joint, so
		-- curved paths have no wedge-shaped collision gaps.
		result = workspace:Spherecast(origin, projectile.Radius, displacement, params)
	else
		result = workspace:Raycast(origin, displacement, params)
	end
	if not result then
		return nil
	end
	return {
		Position = result.Position,
		Normal = result.Normal,
		Instance = result.Instance,
		Distance = result.Distance,
	}
end

-- Does the chunk containing `position` currently hold any entities? Drives the
-- high/low resolution decision each substep.
function Raycast.chunkHasEntities(position: Vector3): boolean
	local chunk = ChunkManager.GetChunk(position)
	return chunk ~= nil and chunk.EntityCount > 0
end

-- Builds the table passed to every projectile.OnHit listener -- see the
-- "Events" section in init.luau. `entity` is nil for a pure world/wall contact.
function Raycast.buildHitInfo(contact: Types.Contact, entity: Types.EntityLike?, hurtbox: Types.Hurtbox?): Types.HitInfo
	local normal = SafeMath.direction(contact.Normal, Vector3.zAxis)
	return {
		CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(contact.Position, contact.Position + normal),
		Part = contact.Instance,
		Entity = entity,
		Hurtbox = hurtbox,
	}
end

-- Steps the projectile just past `surface` along its direction of travel.
function Raycast.nudgePast(projectile: State, surface: Vector3)
	projectile.Position = surface
		+ SafeMath.direction(projectile.Velocity, Vector3.zAxis) * (projectile.Radius + PASS_CLEARANCE)
end
local nudgePast = Raycast.nudgePast

-- Resolves `entity` being struck at `contact` (by a raycast, or by a
-- lag-compensated rewind check -- see RewindHit). "destroy" means the caller
-- must Destroy(contact, "entity").
function Raycast.resolveEntityHit(
	projectile: State,
	entity: Types.EntityLike,
	contact: Types.Contact,
	hurtbox: Types.Hurtbox?
): Verdict
	if entity == projectile.Source or projectile._ignore[entity] then
		-- can't collide with ourselves or an already-pierced target
		nudgePast(projectile, contact.Position)
		return "pass"
	end
	local filter = projectile.Filter
	if filter and not filter(entity) then
		return "fallthrough"
	end

	projectile.OnHit:Fire(Raycast.buildHitInfo(contact, entity, hurtbox))
	if projectile.PiercesLeft > 0 then
		projectile.PiercesLeft -= 1
		projectile.DamageMultiplier *= (1 - projectile.PierceFalloff)
		projectile._ignore[entity] = true
		nudgePast(projectile, contact.Position)
		return "pass"
	end
	return "destroy"
end

-- Attempts to punch this projectile through the wall it just hit. Probes a
-- point Penetration studs further along the ray past the entry point, then
-- raycasts BACKWARD from that probe to the entry point, whitelisted to ONLY
-- the part that was just hit:
--  - Hit: the wall's far/exit surface lies between the probe and the entry
--    point, i.e. the wall is thinner than the remaining budget. The wall's
--    actual thickness (not the probe distance) is subtracted, so a thin wall
--    barely dents the budget and a thick one nearly exhausts it.
--  - Nil: the probe point is still INSIDE the wall (Roblox raycasts never hit
--    a part they start inside), so the wall is thicker than the budget.
-- Returns the position just past the exit surface, or nil if blocked.
local function attemptPenetration(projectile: State, contact: Types.Contact): Vector3?
	local instance = contact.Instance
	if not instance then
		return nil
	end

	local direction = SafeMath.direction(projectile.Velocity, Vector3.zAxis)
	local probeOrigin = contact.Position + direction * projectile.Penetration

	local probeParams = RaycastParams.new()
	probeParams.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Include
	probeParams.FilterDescendantsInstances = { instance }

	local probeResult = workspace:Raycast(probeOrigin, contact.Position - probeOrigin, probeParams)
	if not probeResult then
		return nil
	end

	local thickness = (probeResult.Position - contact.Position).Magnitude
	projectile.Penetration = math.max(projectile.Penetration - thickness, 0)
	return probeResult.Position + direction * (projectile.Radius + PASS_CLEARANCE)
end

-- Resolves a physical cast contact. Returns the verdict and, for "destroy",
-- the kind to Destroy() with. A bounce queues a one-shot ProjMove correction
-- (Bounced = true) -- the ONLY streaming a non-homing bouncing projectile
-- ever gets; it tells rendering clients to snap instead of tween and to
-- re-baseline their local physics (see ProjectileClient).
function Raycast.resolveHit(projectile: State, contact: Types.Contact): (Verdict, string?)
	local instance = contact.Instance
	local entity: Types.EntityLike? = if instance then Entity.Get(instance) else nil

	if entity then
		-- Head/Body classification is purely analytic: the raycast hits
		-- whatever real rig geometry is physically in the way; we just check
		-- whether that hit POINT falls within HeadRadius of the Head center
		-- (see Entity.luau's "Head + Body hurtboxes" section).
		local hurtbox: Types.Hurtbox = "Body"
		local headPosition = entity:GetHeadPosition()
		if headPosition and (contact.Position - headPosition).Magnitude <= entity.HeadRadius then
			hurtbox = "Head"
		end

		local verdict = Raycast.resolveEntityHit(projectile, entity, contact, hurtbox)
		if verdict == "destroy" then
			return "destroy", "entity"
		elseif verdict ~= "fallthrough" then
			-- (cast: Luau widens the refined literal union back to string)
			return verdict :: Verdict, nil
		end
		-- filtered out: treat like world geometry below
	end

	-- Penetration is tried before bouncing; a wall thicker than the remaining
	-- budget falls through to bounce/destroy as if Penetration were 0.
	if projectile.Penetration > 0 then
		local exitPosition = attemptPenetration(projectile, contact)
		if exitPosition then
			projectile.OnHit:Fire(Raycast.buildHitInfo(contact, entity, nil))
			projectile.Position = exitPosition
			return "pass", nil
		end
	end

	if projectile.BouncesLeft > 0 then
		projectile.BouncesLeft -= 1
		local normal = SafeMath.direction(contact.Normal, Vector3.yAxis)
		local velocity = projectile.Velocity
		projectile.Velocity = (velocity - 2 * velocity:Dot(normal) * normal) * projectile.Restitution
		projectile.Position = contact.Position + normal * (projectile.Radius + BOUNCE_CLEARANCE)
		if projectile.Beam and not projectile._spawnStreamed then projectile._beamOrigin = projectile.Position end
		-- Connect the cleared sphere center, not the surface inside its radius.
		if projectile._beamTurns then table.insert(projectile._beamTurns, projectile.Position) end
		-- The client must SNAP on a bounce instead of tweening a straight line
		-- from its pre-bounce position, which would visibly cut through the
		-- surface it bounced off. The snap goes out with this frame's ProjMove
		-- batch (see Replication.queueBounce for why it carries the end-of-frame
		-- pose), even if a later substep this same tick destroys the
		-- projectile; ProjHit is only flushed on a later frame, so the snap
		-- always reaches the client first.
		Replication.queueBounce(projectile, contact.Position, normal)
		local onBounce = projectile.OnBounce
		if onBounce then
			task.spawn(onBounce, projectile, contact)
		end
		projectile.OnHit:Fire(Raycast.buildHitInfo(contact, entity, nil))
		return "bounce", nil
	end

	projectile.OnHit:Fire(Raycast.buildHitInfo(contact, entity, nil))
	return "destroy", "world"
end

return Raycast
-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/server/Projectile/Raycast.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/Occupancy.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!strict
--!native
--!optimize 2
--[[
	Projectile/Occupancy.luau
	Skips movement raycasts through provably empty space. A sweep is only
	skipped when nothing a raycast could hit is anywhere near it, so the result
	is identical to casting (no hit) -- just without the engine call.

	Static geometry (anchored assemblies) is baked into a sparse two-level
	grid: COARSE-stud cells, each holding a 4096-bit mask (a 512-byte buffer)
	of FINE-stud sub-voxels. Masks are interned: a cell points at a shared,
	never-mutated mask (marking copies, edits and re-interns), so the many
	identical cells along a floor or wall cost one table slot each -- which
	matters because every parallel projectile worker bakes its own copy. Every part is marked by its world AABB grown by PAD
	studs, which is what makes a centreline walk safe for sphere sweeps up to
	MaxRadius: any surface within that distance of the path lies in a marked
	voxel on the path. Marks are only ever added (a moved static part is
	re-marked at its new place, never cleared at the old one), so staleness
	can only cost a skipped skip, never a missed hit.

	Parts with CanQuery off are skipped (raycasts can't hit them) until it's
	turned on. A part bigger than REFINE_OVER studs whose shape isn't its box
	(meshes, unions, wedges, balls...) is baked by its real collision geometry:
	its box is split recursively and each piece tested with GetPartsInPart
	(the same geometry raycasts hit), so e.g. a tree's mostly-empty bounding
	box isn't marked solid. While that runs the part counts as dynamic (coarse,
	conservative); the initial bake finishes it before anything is skipped.

	Dynamic geometry -- anything unanchored, and every part of a model with a
	Humanoid (characters, dummies, ragdolls) -- is re-marked at coarse level
	once per physics frame, the first time a query needs it, grown by its
	speed so it can't outrun its mark. New parts count as dynamic from the
	moment they appear (until a deferred check finds them anchored), so a
	part spawned this frame is never skipped past.

	Terrain (any map that has it) is read in background batches with
	ReadVoxels over the area around the map's parts (or a default area for a
	terrain-only map) and marked like parts. While a map has terrain, a path
	that leaves the scanned area always raycasts. Terrain edited at runtime
	isn't detected: call Occupancy.BakeTerrain(min, max) over the edited area
	(marks only add, so removed terrain just stops being skipped through).

	SegmentClear(origin, displacement, radius) walks the path's coarse cells
	(the common case in open air: a handful of empty lookups) and only walks
	fine voxels through cells that have something in them.
]]

local Occupancy = {}

local COARSE = 64 -- studs per coarse cell edge
local FINE = 4 -- studs per sub-voxel edge
local DIV = COARSE // FINE -- sub-voxels per coarse edge (16 -> 4096-bit masks)
local ROW_BYTES = DIV // 8 -- one x-row of a cell (16 bits)
local MASK_BYTES = DIV * DIV * ROW_BYTES -- 512
local PAD = FINE -- studs every part's AABB is grown by
local DYNAMIC_MARGIN = 2 -- extra studs around moving parts
local DYNAMIC_LOOKAHEAD = 1 / 15 -- seconds of travel added around moving parts
local DEMOTE_AFTER_MOVES = 20 -- a static part moved this often is treated as dynamic
local BAKE_BATCH = 400 -- parts baked per resumption
local TERRAIN_BLOCK = 256 -- studs per ReadVoxels block edge (64^3 voxels)
local TERRAIN_AROUND_PARTS = 512 -- studs of terrain scanned beyond the map's parts
local TERRAIN_DEFAULT_MIN = Vector3.new(-2048, -512, -2048) -- terrain-only maps
local TERRAIN_DEFAULT_MAX = Vector3.new(2048, 1024, 2048)
local REFINE_OVER = 32 -- studs: bigger non-box parts are baked by their real shape
local REFINE_SLICE = 0.004 -- seconds of shape probing per resumption

-- Sweeps wider than this always raycast (the padding wouldn't cover them).
Occupancy.MaxRadius = PAD - 0.25
Occupancy.Enabled = true

local OFFSET = 32768
local STRIDE = 65536
local STRIDE2 = STRIDE * STRIDE

local floor, min, max, abs = math.floor, math.min, math.max, math.abs
local bor, btest, lshift = bit32.bor, bit32.btest, bit32.lshift
local readu16, writeu16 = buffer.readu16, buffer.writeu16

local function cellKey(cx: number, cy: number, cz: number): number
	return (cx + OFFSET) + (cy + OFFSET) * STRIDE + (cz + OFFSET) * STRIDE2
end

local static: { [number]: buffer } = {} -- coarse key -> interned sub-voxel mask
local masks: { [string]: buffer } = {} -- mask contents -> the one shared buffer
local FULL = buffer.create(MASK_BYTES)
buffer.fill(FULL, 0, 255)
masks[buffer.tostring(FULL)] = FULL
local scratch = buffer.create(MASK_BYTES)
local dynamic: { [number]: boolean } = {} -- coarse key -> something moving there this frame
local dynamicParts: { [BasePart]: boolean } = {}
local staticMoves: { [BasePart]: number } = {}
local watchedRoots: { [BasePart]: { BasePart } } = {} -- anchored root -> parts welded to it
local dynamicStamp = -1 -- workspace.DistributedGameTime the dynamic marks belong to
local ready = false
-- While the map has terrain: the scanned area; outside it nothing is skipped.
local hasTerrain = false
local terrainMin, terrainMax = Vector3.zero, Vector3.zero

local stats = { Checks = 0, Skipped = 0, Coarse = 0, StaticCells = 0, DistinctMasks = 1, DynamicParts = 0 }

local function intern(mask: buffer): buffer
	local contents = buffer.tostring(mask)
	local existing = masks[contents]
	if existing then
		return existing
	end
	local copy = buffer.fromstring(contents)
	masks[contents] = copy
	stats.DistinctMasks += 1
	return copy
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Marking
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- World AABB of a part's oriented box, grown by `grow`.
local function bounds(part: BasePart, grow: number): (Vector3, Vector3)
	local cf = part.CFrame
	local half = part.Size * 0.5
	local xv, yv, zv = cf.XVector, cf.YVector, cf.ZVector
	local extent = Vector3.new(
		abs(xv.X) * half.X + abs(yv.X) * half.Y + abs(zv.X) * half.Z,
		abs(xv.Y) * half.X + abs(yv.Y) * half.Y + abs(zv.Y) * half.Z,
		abs(xv.Z) * half.X + abs(yv.Z) * half.Y + abs(zv.Z) * half.Z
	) + Vector3.one * grow
	local centre = cf.Position
	return centre - extent, centre + extent
end

-- Sets every sub-voxel overlapping [lo, hi]. Bit (fx + fy*16 + fz*256) is bit
-- fx of the u16 row at (fy + fz*16), so one x-row of a cell is one write.
local function markStatic(lo: Vector3, hi: Vector3)
	local fx0, fy0, fz0 = floor(lo.X / FINE), floor(lo.Y / FINE), floor(lo.Z / FINE)
	local fx1, fy1, fz1 = floor(hi.X / FINE), floor(hi.Y / FINE), floor(hi.Z / FINE)
	for cz = fz0 // DIV, fz1 // DIV do
		local az, bz = max(fz0 - cz * DIV, 0), min(fz1 - cz * DIV, DIV - 1)
		for cy = fy0 // DIV, fy1 // DIV do
			local ay, by = max(fy0 - cy * DIV, 0), min(fy1 - cy * DIV, DIV - 1)
			for cx = fx0 // DIV, fx1 // DIV do
				local ax, bx = max(fx0 - cx * DIV, 0), min(fx1 - cx * DIV, DIV - 1)
				local k = cellKey(cx, cy, cz)
				local current = static[k]
				if current == FULL then
					continue
				end
				if not current then
					stats.StaticCells += 1
				end
				if ax == 0 and bx == DIV - 1 and ay == 0 and by == DIV - 1 and az == 0 and bz == DIV - 1 then
					static[k] = FULL
					continue
				end
				-- shared masks are never edited in place: edit a copy, re-intern
				if current then
					buffer.copy(scratch, 0, current, 0, MASK_BYTES)
				else
					buffer.fill(scratch, 0, 0)
				end
				local row = lshift(lshift(1, bx - ax + 1) - 1, ax)
				for fz = az, bz do
					for fy = ay, by do
						local offset = (fy + fz * DIV) * ROW_BYTES
						writeu16(scratch, offset, bor(readu16(scratch, offset), row))
					end
				end
				static[k] = intern(scratch)
			end
		end
	end
end

local function markDynamicBox(lo: Vector3, hi: Vector3)
	for cz = floor(lo.Z / COARSE), floor(hi.Z / COARSE) do
		for cy = floor(lo.Y / COARSE), floor(hi.Y / COARSE) do
			for cx = floor(lo.X / COARSE), floor(hi.X / COARSE) do
				dynamic[cellKey(cx, cy, cz)] = true
			end
		end
	end
end

-- Re-marks every moving part, once per physics frame (all queries in one
-- Heartbeat see the same world).
local function refreshDynamic()
	local stamp = workspace.DistributedGameTime
	if stamp == dynamicStamp then
		return
	end
	dynamicStamp = stamp
	table.clear(dynamic)
	local count = 0
	for part in dynamicParts do
		if not part.Parent then
			dynamicParts[part] = nil
			continue
		end
		count += 1
		local reach = PAD + DYNAMIC_MARGIN + part.AssemblyLinearVelocity.Magnitude * DYNAMIC_LOOKAHEAD
		local lo, hi = bounds(part, reach)
		markDynamicBox(lo, hi)
	end
	stats.DynamicParts = count
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Classification
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local function inCharacter(part: BasePart): boolean
	local model = part:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
	while model do
		if model:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid") then
			return true
		end
		model = model:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
	end
	return false
end

-- Is this part's collision shape its own box?
local function boxShaped(part: BasePart): boolean
	return part:IsA("Part") and (part :: Part).Shape == Enum.PartType.Block
end

-- The FINE-voxel boxes (lo, hi pairs) of `part`'s real collision geometry,
-- each grown by PAD for the test (so marking them needs no further padding):
-- its box is split into octants on the voxel grid and a piece is kept only
-- if GetPartsInPart finds the part in it. Yields every REFINE_SLICE. nil if
-- the part left the world meanwhile.
local probe = Instance.new("Part")
probe.Anchored = true

local function refineShape(part: BasePart): { Vector3 }?
	local params = OverlapParams.new()
	params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Include
	params.FilterDescendantsInstances = { part }
	local grow = Vector3.one * (2 * PAD)
	local lo, hi = bounds(part, 0)
	lo = Vector3.new(floor(lo.X / FINE) * FINE, floor(lo.Y / FINE) * FINE, floor(lo.Z / FINE) * FINE)
	hi = Vector3.new(math.ceil(hi.X / FINE) * FINE, math.ceil(hi.Y / FINE) * FINE, math.ceil(hi.Z / FINE) * FINE)
	local boxes: { Vector3 } = {}
	local stack: { Vector3 } = { lo, hi }
	local sliceStarted = os.clock()
	-- an axis range split in two on the voxel grid (one range if it's one voxel)
	local function halves(a: number, b: number): { number }
		if b - a <= FINE then
			return { a, b }
		end
		local m = a + math.ceil((b - a) / FINE / 2) * FINE
		return { a, m, m, b }
	end
	while #stack > 0 do
		local nodeHi = table.remove(stack) :: Vector3
		local nodeLo = table.remove(stack) :: Vector3
		if os.clock() - sliceStarted > REFINE_SLICE then
			task.wait()
			sliceStarted = os.clock()
			if not part.Parent then
				return nil
			end
		end
		probe.Size = nodeHi - nodeLo + grow
		probe.CFrame = CFrame.new((nodeLo + nodeHi) * 0.5)
		if #workspace:GetPartsInPart(probe, params) == 0 then
			continue
		end
		local size = nodeHi - nodeLo
		if size.X <= FINE and size.Y <= FINE and size.Z <= FINE then
			table.insert(boxes, nodeLo)
			table.insert(boxes, nodeHi)
			continue
		end
		local xs, ys, zs = halves(nodeLo.X, nodeHi.X), halves(nodeLo.Y, nodeHi.Y), halves(nodeLo.Z, nodeHi.Z)
		for i = 1, #xs, 2 do
			for j = 1, #ys, 2 do
				for k = 1, #zs, 2 do
					table.insert(stack, Vector3.new(xs[i], ys[j], zs[k]))
					table.insert(stack, Vector3.new(xs[i + 1], ys[j + 1], zs[k + 1]))
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return boxes
end

local queryWatched: { [BasePart]: boolean } = {}

local function makeDynamic(part: BasePart)
	if not dynamicParts[part] then
		dynamicParts[part] = true
		dynamicStamp = -1 -- the current frame's marks no longer cover it
	end
end

local classify: (part: BasePart) -> ()

-- A static part moved (or its anchoring changed): mark where it is now, and
-- give up on it as static if it keeps moving or stopped being anchored.
local function staticChanged(part: BasePart)
	if not part.Parent or dynamicParts[part] then
		return
	end
	local root = part.AssemblyRootPart
	if not (part.Anchored or (root and root.Anchored)) then
		makeDynamic(part)
		return
	end
	local moves = (staticMoves[part] or 0) + 1
	staticMoves[part] = moves
	if moves >= DEMOTE_AFTER_MOVES then
		makeDynamic(part)
		return
	end
	local lo, hi = bounds(part, PAD)
	markStatic(lo, hi)
end

local function watchStatic(part: BasePart)
	part:GetPropertyChangedSignal("CFrame"):Connect(function()
		staticChanged(part)
	end)
	part:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Size"):Connect(function()
		staticChanged(part)
	end)
	part:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Anchored"):Connect(function()
		staticChanged(part)
	end)
	-- Parts welded to an anchored root move with it without their own CFrame
	-- signal firing, and become loose if the root is unanchored: watch the root.
	local root = part.AssemblyRootPart
	if root and root ~= part then
		local list = watchedRoots[root]
		if not list then
			list = {}
			watchedRoots[root] = list
			local function rootChanged()
				for _, member in list do
					staticChanged(member)
				end
			end
			root:GetPropertyChangedSignal("CFrame"):Connect(rootChanged)
			root:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Anchored"):Connect(rootChanged)
		end
		table.insert(list, part)
	end
end

function classify(part: BasePart)
	if part:IsA("Terrain") or not part:IsDescendantOf(workspace) then
		return
	end
	if not part.CanQuery then
		-- raycasts can't hit it: nothing to mark until that changes
		dynamicParts[part] = nil
		if not queryWatched[part] then
			queryWatched[part] = true
			part:GetPropertyChangedSignal("CanQuery"):Connect(function()
				if part.CanQuery and part.Parent then
					makeDynamic(part)
					task.spawn(classify, part)
				end
			end)
		end
		return
	end
	local root = part.AssemblyRootPart
	local anchored = part.Anchored or (root ~= nil and root.Anchored)
	if not anchored or inCharacter(part) then
		makeDynamic(part)
		return
	end
	local size = part.Size
	if (size.X > REFINE_OVER or size.Y > REFINE_OVER or size.Z > REFINE_OVER) and not boxShaped(part) then
		makeDynamic(part) -- (conservative while its shape is probed)
		local boxes = refineShape(part)
		if not boxes or not part.Parent then
			return
		end
		local inset = Vector3.one * 0.01 -- (a voxel's far face would also mark its neighbour)
		for index = 1, #boxes, 2 do
			markStatic(boxes[index], boxes[index + 1] - inset)
		end
	else
		local lo, hi = bounds(part, PAD)
		markStatic(lo, hi)
	end
	dynamicParts[part] = nil
	watchStatic(part)
end

-- A joint went away: its parts may now be loose, so stop trusting them as static.
local function jointRemoved(joint: Instance)
	for _, name in { "Part0", "Part1" } do
		local part = (joint :: any)[name]
		if typeof(part) == "Instance" and part:IsA("BasePart") and not part.Anchored then
			makeDynamic(part)
		end
	end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Query
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local function fineOccupied(fx: number, fy: number, fz: number): boolean
	local cx, cy, cz = fx // DIV, fy // DIV, fz // DIV
	local k = cellKey(cx, cy, cz)
	if dynamic[k] then
		return true
	end
	local mask = static[k]
	if not mask then
		return false
	end
	local lx, ly, lz = fx - cx * DIV, fy - cy * DIV, fz - cz * DIV
	return btest(readu16(mask, (ly + lz * DIV) * ROW_BYTES), lshift(1, lx))
end

local function coarseOccupied(cx: number, cy: number, cz: number): boolean
	local k = cellKey(cx, cy, cz)
	return dynamic[k] == true or static[k] ~= nil
end

-- Amanatides-Woo walk of every `size`-stud voxel the segment passes through;
-- true as soon as `occupied` says one is.
local function walk(origin: Vector3, displacement: Vector3, size: number, occupied: (number, number, number) -> boolean): boolean
	local x, y, z = origin.X / size, origin.Y / size, origin.Z / size
	local dx, dy, dz = displacement.X / size, displacement.Y / size, displacement.Z / size
	local ix, iy, iz = floor(x), floor(y), floor(z)
	local ex, ey, ez = floor(x + dx), floor(y + dy), floor(z + dz)
	local sx = if dx > 0 then 1 elseif dx < 0 then -1 else 0
	local sy = if dy > 0 then 1 elseif dy < 0 then -1 else 0
	local sz = if dz > 0 then 1 elseif dz < 0 then -1 else 0
	local inf = math.huge
	local tx = if dx > 0 then (ix + 1 - x) / dx elseif dx < 0 then (x - ix) / -dx else inf
	local ty = if dy > 0 then (iy + 1 - y) / dy elseif dy < 0 then (y - iy) / -dy else inf
	local tz = if dz > 0 then (iz + 1 - z) / dz elseif dz < 0 then (z - iz) / -dz else inf
	local ux = if dx ~= 0 then 1 / abs(dx) else inf
	local uy = if dy ~= 0 then 1 / abs(dy) else inf
	local uz = if dz ~= 0 then 1 / abs(dz) else inf
	local steps = abs(ex - ix) + abs(ey - iy) + abs(ez - iz) + 1
	for _ = 1, steps do
		if occupied(ix, iy, iz) then
			return true
		end
		if tx <= ty and tx <= tz then
			ix += sx
			tx += ux
		elseif ty <= tz then
			iy += sy
			ty += uy
		else
			iz += sz
			tz += uz
		end
	end
	-- floating-point slack: the end voxel is always checked
	return occupied(ex, ey, ez)
end

-- Is the whole segment (plus padding) inside the scanned terrain area?
local function insideTerrainScan(origin: Vector3, finish: Vector3): boolean
	local lo = origin:Min(finish) - Vector3.one * PAD
	local hi = origin:Max(finish) + Vector3.one * PAD
	return lo.X >= terrainMin.X and lo.Y >= terrainMin.Y and lo.Z >= terrainMin.Z
		and hi.X <= terrainMax.X and hi.Y <= terrainMax.Y and hi.Z <= terrainMax.Z
end

-- True when a sweep of `radius` from `origin` along `displacement` provably
-- hits nothing, so the caller can skip its raycast. Conservative: any doubt
-- (not baked yet, too wide, outside scanned terrain, anything near the path)
-- returns false.
function Occupancy.SegmentClear(origin: Vector3, displacement: Vector3, radius: number): boolean
	stats.Checks += 1
	if not ready or not Occupancy.Enabled or radius > Occupancy.MaxRadius then
		return false
	end
	if hasTerrain and not insideTerrainScan(origin, origin + displacement) then
		return false
	end
	refreshDynamic()
	if walk(origin, displacement, COARSE, coarseOccupied) then
		stats.Coarse += 1
		if walk(origin, displacement, FINE, fineOccupied) then
			return false
		end
	end
	stats.Skipped += 1
	return true
end

-- Counters since the last call (DebugService's Stats tab), then reset.
function Occupancy.TakeStats()
	local snapshot = table.clone(stats)
	snapshot.Ready = ready
	stats.Checks, stats.Skipped, stats.Coarse = 0, 0, 0
	return snapshot
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Terrain
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local function snap(value: number, toward: number): number
	return if toward < 0 then floor(value / FINE) * FINE else math.ceil(value / FINE) * FINE
end

-- Reads terrain between `lo` and `hi` in TERRAIN_BLOCK batches (yielding
-- between them) and marks every solid voxel; contiguous x-runs are marked as
-- one box. Water is skipped (projectile rays ignore it).
function Occupancy.BakeTerrain(lo: Vector3, hi: Vector3)
	local terrain = workspace.Terrain
	lo = Vector3.new(snap(lo.X, -1), snap(lo.Y, -1), snap(lo.Z, -1))
	hi = Vector3.new(snap(hi.X, 1), snap(hi.Y, 1), snap(hi.Z, 1))
	local air, water = Enum.Material.Air, Enum.Material.Water
	local pad = Vector3.one * PAD
	for bz = lo.Z, hi.Z - 1, TERRAIN_BLOCK do
		for by = lo.Y, hi.Y - 1, TERRAIN_BLOCK do
			for bx = lo.X, hi.X - 1, TERRAIN_BLOCK do
				local blockLo = Vector3.new(bx, by, bz)
				local blockHi = Vector3.new(min(bx + TERRAIN_BLOCK, hi.X), min(by + TERRAIN_BLOCK, hi.Y), min(bz + TERRAIN_BLOCK, hi.Z))
				local ok, materials = pcall(terrain.ReadVoxels, terrain, Region3.new(blockLo, blockHi), FINE)
				if ok then
					local size = materials.Size
					for z = 1, size.Z do
						for y = 1, size.Y do
							local runStart: number? = nil
							for x = 1, size.X + 1 do
								local material = if x <= size.X then materials[x][y][z] else air
								local solid = material ~= air and material ~= water
								if solid and not runStart then
									runStart = x
								elseif not solid and runStart then
									local voxelLo = blockLo + Vector3.new((runStart - 1) * FINE, (y - 1) * FINE, (z - 1) * FINE)
									local voxelHi = blockLo + Vector3.new((x - 1) * FINE, y * FINE, z * FINE)
									markStatic(voxelLo - pad, voxelHi + pad)
									runStart = nil
								end
							end
						end
					end
				else
					warn("[Projectile] occupancy: terrain read failed, that area stays unscanned:", materials)
				end
				task.wait()
			end
		end
	end
end

-- The area to scan: the map's anchored parts plus a margin, or the default area.
local function terrainScanArea(parts: { BasePart }): (Vector3, Vector3)
	local lo, hi = Vector3.one * math.huge, -Vector3.one * math.huge
	for _, part in parts do
		if part.Parent and part.Anchored then
			lo, hi = lo:Min(part.Position), hi:Max(part.Position)
		end
	end
	if lo.X > hi.X then
		return TERRAIN_DEFAULT_MIN, TERRAIN_DEFAULT_MAX
	end
	local margin = Vector3.one * TERRAIN_AROUND_PARTS
	return lo - margin, hi + margin
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Startup: watch first (so nothing appears unseen), then bake in batches
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

workspace.DescendantAdded:Connect(function(instance)
	if instance:IsA("BasePart") then
		-- dynamic until proven anchored: never skip past a part spawned this frame
		makeDynamic(instance)
		task.defer(function()
			if instance.Parent then
				classify(instance)
			end
		end)
	end
end)
workspace.DescendantRemoving:Connect(function(instance)
	if instance:IsA("BasePart") then
		dynamicParts[instance] = nil
		staticMoves[instance] = nil
		queryWatched[instance] = nil
	elseif instance:IsA("JointInstance") or instance:IsA("WeldConstraint") then
		jointRemoved(instance)
	end
end)

task.spawn(function()
	local started = os.clock()
	local parts = {}
	for _, descendant in workspace:GetDescendants() do
		if descendant:IsA("BasePart") then
			table.insert(parts, descendant)
		end
	end
	for index, part in parts do
		if part.Parent then
			classify(part)
		end
		if index % BAKE_BATCH == 0 then
			task.wait()
		end
	end
	local ok, cells = pcall(function()
		return workspace.Terrain:CountCells()
	end)
	if not ok or cells > 0 then
		hasTerrain = true
		terrainMin, terrainMax = terrainScanArea(parts)
		Occupancy.BakeTerrain(terrainMin, terrainMax)
	end
	ready = true
	print(string.format("[Projectile] occupancy baked: %d parts%s, %d cells, %.0f ms", #parts,
		if hasTerrain then " + terrain" else "", stats.StaticCells, (os.clock() - started) * 1000))
end)

return Occupancy
-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/server/Projectile/Occupancy.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/Homing.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!native
--!strict
--!optimize 2
--[[
	Projectile/Homing.luau
	Target acquisition and steering. Homing.update(projectile, dt) runs once
	per substep from init.luau's Step; it only ever changes the projectile's
	HomingTarget, its homing timers, and the direction of its Velocity.
]]

local Shared = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("Shared")
local ChunkManager = require(Shared:WaitForChild("ChunkManager"))
local Entity = require(Shared:WaitForChild("Entity"))

local Math = require(script.Parent.Math)
local Types = require(script.Parent.Types)

type State = Types.State

local Homing = {}

function Homing.targetPosition(target: Types.HomingTarget?): Vector3?
	if target == nil then
		return nil
	end
	if typeof(target) == "Vector3" then
		return target
	end
	if typeof(target) == "Instance" then
		if target:IsA("BasePart") then
			return target.Position
		elseif target:IsA("Model") then
			return target:GetPivot().Position
		end
		return nil
	end
	-- an Entity
	if target.IsDestroyed then
		return nil
	end
	return target:GetPosition()
end

local function isEligible(projectile: State, homing: Types.Homing, entity: Types.EntityLike): boolean
	if entity == projectile.Source or entity.IsDestroyed then
		return false
	end
	local filter = projectile.Filter
	if filter and not filter(entity) then
		return false
	end
	local tags = homing.TargetTags
	if tags then
		for _, tag in tags do
			if entity:HasTag(tag) then
				return true
			end
		end
		return false
	elseif homing.TargetTag then
		return entity:HasTag(homing.TargetTag)
	end
	return true
end

-- Finds the nearest valid homing target: entities matching TargetTag/TargetTags
-- (or ALL entities if neither given), excluding the projectile's own Source and
-- anything its Filter rejects. Uses ChunkManager's spatial index when
-- AcquireRadius is set (the normal case -- every real spawn site sets one), so
-- cost scales with local entity density, not total entity/projectile count; the
-- unbounded case (rare) falls back to a full scan.
function Homing.acquireTarget(projectile: State, homing: Types.Homing, position: Vector3): Types.EntityLike?
	local function eligible(entity: Types.EntityLike): boolean
		return isEligible(projectile, homing, entity)
	end

	local radius = homing.AcquireRadius
	local candidates: { Types.EntityLike }
	local bestDistance = math.huge
	if radius then
		candidates = ChunkManager.GetEntitiesInRadius(position, radius, { Filter = eligible })
		bestDistance = radius
	else
		candidates = {}
		local pool = if homing.TargetTag then Entity.GetTagged(homing.TargetTag) else Entity.GetAll()
		for _, entity in pool do
			if eligible(entity) then
				table.insert(candidates, entity)
			end
		end
	end

	local best: Types.EntityLike? = nil
	for _, entity in candidates do
		local distance = (entity:GetPosition() - position).Magnitude
		if distance <= bestDistance then
			best, bestDistance = entity, distance
		end
	end
	return best
end

function Homing.update(projectile: State, dt: number)
	local homing = projectile.Homing
	if not homing then
		return
	end

	if projectile.HomingDelay > 0 then
		projectile.HomingDelay -= dt
		return
	end

	-- (re)acquire a target when none / auto-targeting
	local target = projectile.HomingTarget
	local targetGone = target == nil or Homing.targetPosition(target) == nil

	if targetGone then
		if homing.AcquireRadius or homing.TargetTag or homing.TargetTags then
			projectile._acquireTimer -= dt
			if projectile._acquireTimer <= 0 then
				-- Jittered so a burst fired on one frame spreads its searches
				-- across frames instead of spiking together forever.
				projectile._acquireTimer = homing.AcquireInterval * (0.5 + math.random())
				target = Homing.acquireTarget(projectile, homing, projectile.Position)
				projectile.HomingTarget = target
			end
		end
	elseif not homing.Permalock and homing.Retarget then
		projectile.ReacquireTimer -= dt
		if projectile.ReacquireTimer <= 0 then
			projectile.ReacquireTimer = homing.ReacquireRate
			-- No `or target` fallback: if nothing is in range anymore, the lock
			-- is genuinely dropped. Homing.Permalock (checked above) is the
			-- explicit opt-in for "never drop a lock due to range."
			target = Homing.acquireTarget(projectile, homing, projectile.Position)
			projectile.HomingTarget = target
		end
	end

	local goal = Homing.targetPosition(target)
	if not goal then
		return
	end
	local speed = projectile.Velocity.Magnitude
	local newDirection = Math.rotateTowards(projectile.Velocity, goal - projectile.Position, homing.TurnRate * dt)
	projectile.Velocity = newDirection * speed
end

return Homing
-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/server/Projectile/Homing.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/RewindHit.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!native
--!strict
--!optimize 2
--[[
	Projectile/RewindHit.luau
	Lag-compensated ("rewound") entity hit detection -- the authoritative hit
	check for any shot fired with RewindSeconds > 0 (see Shooter.server.luau),
	which in practice is almost every real networked shot.

	RewindHit.check only answers "which entity, if any, does this segment hit
	from the shooter's point of view"; resolving what the hit does (pierce,
	destroy, events) is Raycast.resolveEntityHit's job.
]]
