local Shared = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("Shared")
local Entity = require(Shared:WaitForChild("Entity"))
local ChunkManager = require(Shared:WaitForChild("ChunkManager"))
local SafeMath = require(Shared:WaitForChild("SafeMath"))

local Math = require(script.Parent.Math)
local Types = require(script.Parent.Types)

type State = Types.State

type Candidate = {
	entity: Types.EntityLike,
	point: Vector3,
	distAlong: number,
	hurtbox: Types.Hurtbox,
}

local RewindHit = {}

-- Reused by every check (the server step is single-threaded, and each check
-- drains it before returning) to avoid per-substep allocation churn.
local candidates: { Candidate } = {}

local function byDistance(a: Candidate, b: Candidate): boolean
	return a.distAlong < b.distAlong
end

-- Lag-compensated entity check for one movement substep. Only meaningful while
-- passing through a chunk that contains entities (see `highRes` in init.luau's
-- Step) and only for shots that carry a positive RewindSeconds. Builds its
-- hurtbox whitelist directly from the (loaded) chunk(s) the segment touches --
-- not a radius sweep -- so a projectile only ever considers entities actually
-- in a loaded chunk it's in, per-shooter-desync.
--
-- Two memoization/deferral choices preserve the exact "nearest in-range entity
-- with a clear LOS to `from`" semantics while cutting redundant work:
--  - The rewind instant (os.clock() - RewindSeconds) is pinned for the whole
--    Step (see init.luau), and each entity's rewound position is memoized in
--    projectile._rewindCache, so an entity rewinds once per frame rather than
--    once per substep.
--  - LOS verification is deferred: in-range candidates are sorted nearest
--    first and LOS-checked in that order, so the raycast count is the rank of
--    the nearest clear candidate rather than every candidate.
-- Returns entity, contact point, surface normal, hurtbox -- or nil.
function RewindHit.check(
	projectile: State,
	from: Vector3,
	to: Vector3
): (Types.EntityLike?, Vector3?, Vector3?, Types.Hurtbox?)
	local whitelist: { [Types.EntityLike]: boolean } = {}
	for _, position in { from, to } do
		local chunk = ChunkManager.GetChunk(position)
		if chunk and ChunkManager.IsChunkActive(chunk) then
			for entity in chunk.Entities do
				whitelist[entity] = true
			end
		end
	end

	-- Each entity is tested against BOTH its rewound Head and Body spheres --
	-- Head is checked first and wins outright if in range (the two spheres
	-- are independent, not required to nest -- see Entity.luau).
	local filter = projectile.Filter
	local cache = projectile._rewindCache
	for entity in whitelist do
		if entity ~= projectile.Source and not projectile._ignore[entity] and (not filter or filter(entity)) then
			local rewound = cache[entity]
			if not rewound then
				rewound = {
					Body = entity:GetBodyPositionAt(projectile._rewindTime),
					Head = entity:GetHeadPositionAt(projectile._rewindTime),
				}
				cache[entity] = rewound
			end

			local head = rewound.Head
			local matchedHead = false
			if head then
				local closest, distance = Math.closestPointOnSegment(head, from, to)
				if distance <= entity.HeadRadius + projectile.Radius then
					local candidate: Candidate = {
						entity = entity,
						point = closest,
						distAlong = (closest - from).Magnitude,
						hurtbox = "Head",
					}
					table.insert(candidates, candidate)
					matchedHead = true
				end
			end
			if not matchedHead then
				local closest, distance = Math.closestPointOnSegment(rewound.Body, from, to)
				if distance <= entity.HitboxRadius + projectile.Radius then
					local candidate: Candidate = {
						entity = entity,
						point = closest,
						distAlong = (closest - from).Magnitude,
						hurtbox = "Body",
					}
					table.insert(candidates, candidate)
				end
			end
		end
	end

	table.sort(candidates, byDistance)

	for _, candidate in candidates do
		-- line-of-sight: real geometry must not block the shot before it would
		-- reach this point, so stale rewound data can never be used to hit
		-- someone through a wall. The hit instance must not belong to the
		-- candidate itself, so a target's own body can't block hitting it.
		local los = workspace:Raycast(from, candidate.point - from, projectile._rayParams)
		local blocked = los ~= nil
			and (los.Position - from).Magnitude < candidate.distAlong - 0.5
			and Entity.Get(los.Instance) ~= candidate.entity
		if not blocked then
			table.clear(candidates)
			return candidate.entity,
				candidate.point,
				SafeMath.direction(from - candidate.point, Vector3.yAxis),
				candidate.hurtbox
		end
	end

	table.clear(candidates)
	return nil, nil, nil, nil
end

return RewindHit
-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/server/Projectile/RewindHit.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/Replication.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!strict
--!optimize 2
--[[
	Projectile/Replication.luau
	Everything that pushes projectile state from the server to rendering
	clients (see ProjectileClient in ReplicatedStorage.Shared for the
	receiving side, and Shared.ProjectileProtocol for the wire format). The
	server stays authoritative; this module only ever sends -- see the
	top-level Projectile doc comment (init.luau) for the protocol's design.

	Per frame, init.luau's step loop calls, in order:
	 flushHitBatch                   (start of frame, bounded)
	 Step -> updateTimeScale / updateSyncState / queueBounce / queueHit
	 queuePose -> refine/collide beam links
	 flushSpawnBatch                 (completed snapshots, bounded)
	 flushMoveBatch                   (end of frame, bounded round-robin)
]]

local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local Shared = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("Shared")
local VisualOffload = require(Shared:WaitForChild("VisualOffload"))
local Protocol = require(Shared:WaitForChild("ProjectileProtocol"))
local Codec = require(Shared:WaitForChild("ProjectileCodec"))
local Heartbeat = require(Shared:WaitForChild("Heartbeat"))

local Types = require(script.Parent.Types)

type State = Types.State

local Channels = Protocol.Channels

local Replication = {}

-- Bounded per-frame work so one client event never grows without bound.
local MAX_SPAWNS_PER_FRAME = 1000
local MAX_HITS_PER_FRAME = 1000
-- Homing poses are round-robined past this; the cursor advances in real frame
-- order and is never reset by dilation, so changing GlobalTimeScale cannot
-- merge staggered cohorts into one spike.
local MAX_POSES_PER_FRAME = 2500
-- Beam geometry is reconstructed locally. Ballistic safety snapshots are
-- sparse; homing and topology/clipping/time changes are never rate-throttled.
local BEAM_REFRESH = 0.5
local beamSnapshots: { [number]: any } = {}

local function rememberBeam(projectile: State, now: number)
	if not projectile.Beam then return end
	beamSnapshots[projectile.Id] = {
		Time = now, PreviousId = projectile.Beam.PreviousId or 0,
		Clipped = projectile._beamSpanClipped == true,
		Path = table.clone(projectile._beamSpan or {}),
		Scale = Heartbeat.GetGlobalTimeScale(), PersonalScale = projectile._lastStreamedTimeScale,
	}
end

local function beamDue(projectile: State, now: number): boolean
	if projectile.HomingTarget then return true end
	local previous = beamSnapshots[projectile.Id]
	if not previous then return true end
	if previous.PreviousId ~= (projectile.Beam.PreviousId or 0)
		or previous.Clipped ~= (projectile._beamSpanClipped == true)
		or previous.Scale ~= Heartbeat.GetGlobalTimeScale()
		or previous.PersonalScale ~= projectile._lastStreamedTimeScale then return true end
	local path = projectile._beamSpan or {}
	if #path ~= #previous.Path then return true end
	-- Bend vertices and clipped endpoints are world anchors, not predictions.
	for index = 2, #path - (if projectile._beamSpanClipped then 0 else 1) do
		if (path[index] - previous.Path[index]).Magnitude > 0.05 then return true end
	end
	return now - previous.Time >= BEAM_REFRESH
end

-- When on, prints every ProjSpawn/ProjSync/ProjTimeScale/ProjHit as it is
-- streamed (individually rare enough to log one line each), plus a
-- once-a-second rate summary for ProjMove. Toggled via Projectile.SetDebugSync.
Replication.DebugSync = false

-- One queued, range-limited message payload.
type Entry = {
	Range: number,
	Position: Vector3,
	Payload: any,
	Recipients: { [Player]: boolean }?,
	Chunk: buffer?, -- Payload encoded once (binary channels), shared by every recipient
}

type BounceSnap = {
	Projectile: State,
	Point: Vector3,
	Normal: Vector3,
	Corrected: boolean?,
}

local spawnQueue: { State } = {}
local spawnQueueHead = 1
local hitQueue: { Entry } = {}
local hitQueueHead = 1
local pendingBounces: { BounceSnap } = {} -- flushed with this frame's ProjMove
local pendingBounceHead = 1
local poseCandidates: { State } = {} -- homing and beam correction candidates
local poseCursor = 1
local moveStats = { batches = 0, entries = 0 }
local beamStats = { Candidates = 0, Updates = 0 }

-- Only finite-range visuals need interest bookkeeping. Unlimited-range
-- stress tests retain the broadcast fast path. The persistent cursor limits
-- re-entry checks independently of simulation/dilation and spawn cohorts.
local interests: { [number]: { Projectile: State, Observers: { [Player]: boolean } } } = {}
local interestOrder: { number } = {}
local interestCursor = 1
local interestCount = 0
local frameRoots: { [Player]: BasePart }? = nil

local function playerRoots(): { [Player]: BasePart }
	local roots: { [Player]: BasePart } = {}
	for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
		local character = player.Character
		local root = character and character.PrimaryPart
		if root then
			roots[player] = root
		end
	end
	return roots
end

-- Sends each entry to every player within its Range (everyone when the range
-- is unlimited), as ONE event per recipient no matter how many entries.
-- With `encode` (ProjMove / ProjHitBatch -- see ProjectileCodec) each entry is
-- encoded once and every recipient's message is one packed buffer of them.
local function fanOut(channel: string, entries: { Entry }, encode: ((any) -> buffer)?)
	if #entries == 0 then
		return
	end
	local function item(entry: Entry): any
		if not encode then
			return entry.Payload
		end
		local chunk = entry.Chunk
		if not chunk then
			chunk = encode(entry.Payload)
			entry.Chunk = chunk
		end
		return chunk
	end
	local function message(list: { any }): any
		return if encode then Codec.Join(list) else list
	end
	local broadcast: { any } = {}
	local perPlayer: { [Player]: { any } } = {}
	local roots: { [Player]: BasePart }? = nil
	for _, entry in entries do
		if entry.Recipients then
			for player in entry.Recipients do
				if not player.Parent then continue end
				local list = perPlayer[player] or {}
				perPlayer[player] = list
				table.insert(list, item(entry))
			end
		elseif entry.Range >= math.huge then
			table.insert(broadcast, item(entry))
		else
			roots = roots or playerRoots()
			for player, root in roots :: { [Player]: BasePart } do
				if (root.Position - entry.Position).Magnitude <= entry.Range then
					local list = perPlayer[player]
					if not list then
						list = {}
						perPlayer[player] = list
					end
					table.insert(list, item(entry))
				end
			end
		end
	end
	if #broadcast > 0 then
		VisualOffload.Fire(channel, message(broadcast))
	end
	for player, list in perPlayer do
		VisualOffload.FireClient(player, channel, message(list))
	end
end

-- Sends one immediate (unbatched) message about `projectile`.
local function streamTo(projectile: State, channel: string, payload: any)
	if not projectile.Visualize then
		return
	end
	-- State changes that happen while a visual is still waiting in the bounded
	-- spawn queue are folded into its eventual spawn snapshot. Sending them
	-- first would create out-of-order client state for visuals not built yet.
	if not projectile._spawnStreamed then
		return
	end
	if projectile.VisualRange >= math.huge then
		VisualOffload.Fire(channel, payload)
		return
	end
	local interest = interests[projectile.Id]
	for player in interest and interest.Observers or {} do
		if player.Parent then
			VisualOffload.FireClient(player, channel, payload)
		end
	end
end

-- Ordinary homing retains its pose stream. Beam endpoints are predicted at
-- one common client epoch, with sparse ballistic snapshots and immediate
-- authoritative steering/topology/clipping/bounce corrections.
function Replication.isSynced(projectile: State): boolean
	return projectile.HomingTarget ~= nil and projectile.Beam == nil
end

-- Fields equal to ProjectileClient's defaults are omitted: remote events
-- serialize every key name per entry, so at batch sizes the defaults were most
-- of the spawn bandwidth.
local function spawnPayload(projectile: State): Protocol.SpawnPayload
	local payload: Protocol.SpawnPayload = {
		Id = projectile.Id,
		Position = projectile.Position,
		Velocity = projectile.Velocity,
		Lifetime = math.max(projectile.Lifetime - projectile.Age, 0),
		MaxRealLifetime = math.max(projectile.MaxRealLifetime - (os.clock() - projectile._spawnRealTime), 0),
		AccelerationDirection = projectile.AccelerationDirection,
		Model = projectile.Model,
		Visual = projectile.Visual,
	}
	if projectile.Gravity ~= 0 then payload.Gravity = projectile.Gravity end
	if projectile.Acceleration ~= 0 then payload.Acceleration = projectile.Acceleration end
	if projectile.MinSpeed ~= 0 then payload.MinSpeed = projectile.MinSpeed end
	if projectile.MaxSpeed ~= math.huge then payload.MaxSpeed = projectile.MaxSpeed end
	if Replication.isSynced(projectile) then payload.Synced = true end
	if projectile._lastStreamedTimeScale ~= 1 then payload.TimeScale = projectile._lastStreamedTimeScale end
	if projectile.VisualScale ~= 1 then payload.VisualScale = projectile.VisualScale end
	if projectile.Beam then
		payload.ServerTime = workspace:GetServerTimeNow()
		payload.GlobalScale = Heartbeat.GetGlobalTimeScale()
		payload.Beam = { Length = projectile.Beam.Length, Radius = projectile.Radius,
			Origin = if projectile.Beam.ChannelId then projectile.Position else projectile._beamOrigin or projectile.Position,
			ChannelId = projectile.Beam.ChannelId, PreviousId = projectile.Beam.PreviousId,
			Path = projectile._beamSpan, Clipped = projectile._beamSpanClipped }
	end
	if projectile.DestroyDelay ~= 0 then payload.DestroyDelay = projectile.DestroyDelay end
	if not projectile.WaitForParticles then payload.WaitForParticles = false end
	if not projectile.WaitForTrails then payload.WaitForTrails = false end
	if projectile.ActivateParticlesOnCreate then payload.ActivateParticlesOnCreate = true end
	return payload
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lifecycle messages
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Queues the visual's creation; it spawns from its latest pose when flushed.
function Replication.spawnVisual(projectile: State)
	if not projectile.Visualize then
		return
	end
	if Replication.DebugSync then
		print(`[Relativity][sync] queued ProjSpawn Id={projectile.Id} Synced={Replication.isSynced(projectile)}`)
	end
	table.insert(spawnQueue, projectile)
end

-- Destruction is queued for the same reason creation is: a mass expiry must
-- become a few bounded batch messages, not thousands of individual remote
-- invocations in one frame. A projectile that dies before its queued spawn
-- was streamed needs no hit message because no client visual exists yet.
function Replication.queueHit(projectile: State, info: Types.DestroyInfo)
	beamSnapshots[projectile.Id] = nil
	if Replication.DebugSync then
		print(`[Relativity][sync] ProjHit Id={projectile.Id} Kind={info.Kind or "fizzle"}`)
	end
	if not projectile.Visualize or not projectile._spawnStreamed then
		return
	end
	local payload: Protocol.HitPayload = {
		Id = projectile.Id,
		Position = info.Position,
		Normal = info.Normal,
		Kind = info.Kind,
		BeamBody = projectile._beamBodyHit,
		BeamPath = projectile._beamSpan,
		BeamClipped = projectile._beamSpanClipped,
	}
	local interest = interests[projectile.Id]
	table.insert(hitQueue, { Range = projectile.VisualRange, Position = info.Position, Payload = payload,
		Recipients = interest and table.clone(interest.Observers) })
	interests[projectile.Id] = nil
	if interest then interestCount -= 1 end
end

-- Compacts a head-indexed queue once its consumed prefix dominates it.
local function compact<T>(queue: { T }, head: number): ({ T }, number)
	if head > #queue then
		table.clear(queue)
		return queue, 1
	elseif head > 4096 and head > #queue / 2 then
		return table.move(queue, head, #queue, 1, {}), 1
	end
	return queue, head
end

function Replication.flushHitBatch()
	local batch: { Entry } = {}
	local last = math.min(#hitQueue, hitQueueHead + MAX_HITS_PER_FRAME - 1)
	for index = hitQueueHead, last do
		table.insert(batch, hitQueue[index])
	end
	hitQueue, hitQueueHead = compact(hitQueue, last + 1)
	fanOut(Channels.HitBatch, batch, Codec.EncodeHit)
end

-- Sends at most MAX_SPAWNS_PER_FRAME new visuals per frame, combined into one
-- RemoteEvent per recipient. Simulation starts immediately on the server;
-- queued visuals spawn from their latest authoritative pose, so batching never
-- rewinds or slows gameplay.
function Replication.flushSpawnBatch()
	frameRoots = playerRoots()
	local batch: { Entry } = {}
	local exits: { [Player]: { number } } = {}
	local remaining = MAX_SPAWNS_PER_FRAME
	local last = math.min(#spawnQueue, spawnQueueHead + remaining - 1)
	for index = spawnQueueHead, last do
		local projectile = spawnQueue[index]
		if projectile.Dead then continue end
		projectile._spawnStreamed = true
		local payload = spawnPayload(projectile)
		projectile._streamedSynced = payload.Synced == true
		rememberBeam(projectile, workspace:GetServerTimeNow())
		local recipients
		if projectile.VisualRange < math.huge then
			recipients = {}
			for player, root in frameRoots :: { [Player]: BasePart } do
				if (root.Position-projectile.Position).Magnitude <= projectile.VisualRange then recipients[player] = true end
			end
			interests[projectile.Id] = { Projectile = projectile, Observers = recipients }
			interestCount += 1
			table.insert(interestOrder, projectile.Id)
		end
		table.insert(batch, { Range = projectile.VisualRange, Position = projectile.Position, Payload = payload, Recipients = recipients })
		remaining -= 1
	end
	spawnQueue, spawnQueueHead = compact(spawnQueue, last + 1)
	-- At most 2500 checks and 1000 creation/re-entry snapshots in a frame.
	-- Hysteresis prevents churn when the player sits on the range boundary.
	for _ = 1, math.min(#interestOrder, MAX_POSES_PER_FRAME) do
		if interestCursor > #interestOrder then interestCursor = 1 end
		local id = interestOrder[interestCursor]
		interestCursor += 1
		local interest = interests[id]
		if not interest then continue end
		local projectile, observers = interest.Projectile, interest.Observers
		local entering: { [Player]: boolean } = {}
		for player in observers do
			local root = (frameRoots :: { [Player]: BasePart })[player]
			if not root or (root.Position-projectile.Position).Magnitude > projectile.VisualRange*1.1+8 then
				observers[player] = nil
				if player.Parent then
					local list = exits[player] or {}; exits[player] = list
					table.insert(list, id)
				end
			end
		end
		for player, root in frameRoots :: { [Player]: BasePart } do
			if not observers[player] and remaining > 0 and (root.Position-projectile.Position).Magnitude <= projectile.VisualRange then
				entering[player], observers[player] = true, true
			end
		end
		if next(entering) then
			table.insert(batch, { Range = projectile.VisualRange, Position = projectile.Position,
				Payload = spawnPayload(projectile), Recipients = entering })
			remaining -= 1
		end
	end
	for player, ids in exits do VisualOffload.FireClient(player, Channels.RangeExit, ids) end
	fanOut(Channels.SpawnBatch, batch)
	if #interestOrder > 4096 and #interestOrder > 2*interestCount then
		local ordered = {}
		for offset = 0, #interestOrder-1 do
			local id = interestOrder[(interestCursor+offset-1)%#interestOrder+1]
			if interests[id] then table.insert(ordered,id) end
		end
		interestOrder, interestCursor = ordered, 1
	end
end
function Replication.getQueueStats()
	return {
		VisualSpawnsPerFrame = MAX_SPAWNS_PER_FRAME,
		VisualHitsPerFrame = MAX_HITS_PER_FRAME,
		PendingVisualSpawns = math.max(#spawnQueue - spawnQueueHead + 1, 0),
		PendingVisualHits = math.max(#hitQueue - hitQueueHead + 1, 0),
		BeamPoseCandidates = beamStats.Candidates,
		BeamPoseUpdates = beamStats.Updates,
		BeamRefreshInterval = BEAM_REFRESH,
		BeamHomingRefreshInterval = 0,
	}
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- State changes (sent immediately, only when something actually changed)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Tells clients the combined Source.TimeScale * projectile.TimeScale only
-- when it CHANGES -- see the "Local time" section in init.luau. In the common
-- case (nobody touches it after firing) this never fires after spawn.
function Replication.updateTimeScale(projectile: State, combinedScale: number)
	if combinedScale == projectile._lastStreamedTimeScale then
		return
	end
	projectile._lastStreamedTimeScale = combinedScale
	if Replication.DebugSync then
		print(`[Relativity][sync] ProjTimeScale Id={projectile.Id} TimeScale={combinedScale}`)
	end
	local payload: Protocol.TimeScalePayload = { Id = projectile.Id, TimeScale = combinedScale }
	streamTo(projectile, Channels.TimeScale, payload)
end

-- Tells clients only when the homing-sync state actually changed. True
-- switches the client into "trust the continuous ProjMove stream" mode; false
-- switches it back to local physics. The authoritative pose rides on this
-- message: it is sent immediately (mid-step) over the same ordered remote as
-- ProjMove, so a separate end-of-frame pose would arrive after the client had
-- already left synced mode and be discarded -- and the round-robin cap could
-- skip it entirely.
function Replication.updateSyncState(projectile: State)
	local synced = Replication.isSynced(projectile)
	if synced == projectile._streamedSynced then
		return
	end
	projectile._streamedSynced = synced
	if Replication.DebugSync then
		print(`[Relativity][sync] ProjSync Id={projectile.Id} Synced={synced}`)
	end
	local payload: Protocol.SyncPayload = {
		Id = projectile.Id,
		Synced = synced,
		Position = projectile.Position,
		Velocity = projectile.Velocity,
	}
	streamTo(projectile, Channels.Sync, payload)
end

-- Debug visualization of one movement cast (see Projectile.SetDebugRays).
function Replication.streamRay(projectile: State, from: Vector3, to: Vector3, lowRes: boolean)
	local payload: Protocol.RayPayload = { From = from, To = to, LowRes = lowRes }
	streamTo(projectile, Channels.Ray, payload)
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Pose stream (ProjMove)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- One-shot bounce snap (see Raycast.resolveHit). Queued rather than fired so
-- a volley bouncing off one floor costs one event per recipient, not one per
-- projectile. Ordering still holds: this frame's flushMoveBatch sends it, and
-- any ProjHit for the same projectile is flushed at the start of a LATER frame.
-- Only the contact point/normal are captured now; the snapped pose is read at
-- flush time, i.e. the end-of-frame pose, the same time base as ProjSpawn and
-- the homing stream. A mid-frame pose would leave the client behind by the
-- rest of the frame the server kept simulating after the bounce.
function Replication.queueBounce(projectile: State, point: Vector3, normal: Vector3)
	if not projectile.Visualize or not projectile._spawnStreamed then
		return
	end
	table.insert(pendingBounces, { Projectile = projectile, Point = point, Normal = normal })
end

function Replication.queueCorrection(projectile: State, point: Vector3, normal: Vector3)
	if not projectile.Visualize or not projectile._spawnStreamed then return end
	table.insert(pendingBounces, { Projectile = projectile, Point = point, Normal = normal, Corrected = true })
end

-- Collects homing/beam candidates. Beam cadence and topology are checked AFTER
-- link refinement; payloads are built only for the bounded slice actually sent.
function Replication.queuePose(projectile: State)
	if projectile.Visualize and projectile._spawnStreamed and (projectile._streamedSynced or projectile.Beam ~= nil) then
		table.insert(poseCandidates, projectile)
	end
end

local function poseEntry(projectile: State): Entry
	local payload: Protocol.MovePayload = {
		Id = projectile.Id,
		Position = projectile.Position,
		Velocity = projectile.Velocity,
		BeamPath = projectile._beamSpan,
		BeamClipped = projectile._beamSpanClipped,
		BeamPreviousId = if projectile.Beam then projectile.Beam.PreviousId or 0 else nil,
		ServerTime = if projectile.Beam then workspace:GetServerTimeNow() else nil,
		GlobalScale = if projectile.Beam then Heartbeat.GetGlobalTimeScale() else nil,
		TimeScale = if projectile.Beam then projectile._lastStreamedTimeScale else nil,
		Lifetime = if projectile.Beam then math.max(projectile.Lifetime-projectile.Age, 0) else nil,
	}
	local interest = interests[projectile.Id]
	return { Range = projectile.VisualRange, Position = projectile.Position, Payload = payload,
		Recipients = if projectile.VisualRange < math.huge then interest and interest.Observers or {} else nil }
end

-- Sends this frame's bounce snaps plus a bounded round-robin slice of the
-- queued homing poses, as one ProjMove event per recipient.
function Replication.flushMoveBatch()
	local batch: { Entry } = {}
	local now = workspace:GetServerTimeNow()
	local sent: { [number]: boolean } = {}
	local lastBounce = math.min(#pendingBounces, pendingBounceHead+MAX_POSES_PER_FRAME-1)
	for index = pendingBounceHead, lastBounce do
		local bounce = pendingBounces[index]
		local projectile = bounce.Projectile
		local payload: Protocol.MovePayload = {
			Id = projectile.Id,
			Position = projectile.Position,
			Velocity = projectile.Velocity,
			Bounced = if bounce.Corrected then nil else true,
			Corrected = bounce.Corrected,
			BeamPreviousId = if projectile.Beam then projectile.Beam.PreviousId or 0 else nil,
			ServerTime = if projectile.Beam then now else nil,
			GlobalScale = if projectile.Beam then Heartbeat.GetGlobalTimeScale() else nil,
			TimeScale = if projectile.Beam then projectile._lastStreamedTimeScale else nil,
			BeamPath = projectile._beamSpan,
			BeamClipped = projectile._beamSpanClipped,
			Lifetime = if projectile.Beam then math.max(projectile.Lifetime-projectile.Age, 0) else nil,
			Point = bounce.Point,
			Normal = bounce.Normal,
		}
		local interest = interests[projectile.Id]
		sent[projectile.Id] = true
		if projectile.Beam then beamStats.Updates += 1 end
		if not projectile.Dead then rememberBeam(projectile, now) end
		table.insert(batch, { Range = projectile.VisualRange, Position = projectile.Position, Payload = payload,
			Recipients = if projectile.VisualRange < math.huge then interest and interest.Observers or {} else nil })
	end
	pendingBounces, pendingBounceHead = compact(pendingBounces, lastBounce+1)

	local due = {}
	for _, projectile in poseCandidates do
		if projectile.Beam then beamStats.Candidates += 1 end
		if not projectile.Dead and not sent[projectile.Id]
			and (not projectile.Beam or beamDue(projectile, now)) then table.insert(due, projectile) end
	end
	table.clear(poseCandidates)
	local candidateCount = #due
	if candidateCount > 0 then
		local updateCount = math.min(candidateCount, math.max(MAX_POSES_PER_FRAME-#batch, 0))
		if poseCursor > candidateCount then
			poseCursor = (poseCursor - 1) % candidateCount + 1
		end
		for offset = 0, updateCount - 1 do
			local projectile = due[(poseCursor + offset - 1) % candidateCount + 1]
			table.insert(batch, poseEntry(projectile))
			if projectile.Beam then beamStats.Updates += 1 end
			rememberBeam(projectile, now)
		end
		poseCursor = (poseCursor + updateCount - 1) % candidateCount + 1
	else
		poseCursor = 1
	end

	if Replication.DebugSync and #batch > 0 then
		moveStats.batches += 1
		moveStats.entries += #batch
	end
	fanOut(Channels.Move, batch, Codec.EncodeMove)
end

-- Once-a-second ProjMove rate summary (see DebugSync) -- real time, not
-- dilated, so the reporting cadence stays steady even mid-freeze.
task.spawn(function()
	while true do
		task.wait(1)
		if Replication.DebugSync and moveStats.batches > 0 then
			print(`[Relativity][sync] ProjMove rate: {moveStats.batches} batches/s, {moveStats.entries} projectile-updates/s`)
		end
		moveStats.batches = 0
		moveStats.entries = 0
	end
end)

return Replication
-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/server/Projectile/Replication.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/Store.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!strict
--!native
--!optimize 2
--[[
	Projectile/Store.luau
	The hot half of every live projectile, packed into one buffer.

	A projectile is still the table Projectile.new returns, and every field
	reads and writes as before (projectile.Position, projectile.Velocity = v,
	projectile.Dead, ...). But the fields touched every frame live in a 64-byte
	record here instead of in the table, behind the table's metatable. The
	per-frame loops (Parallel's dispatch/apply, the server step loop) read the
	records directly, so a projectile that just flies never has its table
	touched -- a 45-field table is ~2 KB of scattered hash nodes, and at
	100k+ projectiles each field read was roughly a cache miss.

	Record (STRIDE bytes, slot * STRIDE):
	   0  Position        3 x f32 (Vector3 is float32, so this is exact)
	  12  Velocity        3 x f32
	  24  Age             f64
	  32  _simulationDebt f64
	  40  TimeScale       f64 (its OWN scale; non-numbers are stored as 1, which
	                           is what combinedTimeScale made of them anyway)
	  48  _sweepMark      f64 (0 when unset)
	  56  Source          u32 index into a refcounted source list (0: none)
	  60  flags           u8  (Dead, Dirty, _spawnStreamed, _streamedSynced, and
	                           Visualize / Beam ~= nil, fixed at adopt)

	Dirty is set by any write of a motion field (Position, Velocity, Age,
	_simulationDebt, TimeScale, Dead) through the table: it tells Parallel the
	worker's copy is stale, instead of comparing every field per frame.
	Parallel clears it when it repacks the projectile.

	Lifetime: adopt() moves a new table's hot fields in; release() (when the
	step loop drops it from `active`) copies them back out as plain fields, so
	a handle a caller kept keeps working, and frees the slot. Generation[slot]
	counts releases, so a stale reference to a reused slot can be recognised.
]]

local Store = {}

local STRIDE = 64
local POSITION, VELOCITY, AGE, DEBT, SCALE, MARK, SOURCE, FLAGS = 0, 12, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 60

Store.Stride = STRIDE
Store.Position, Store.Velocity, Store.Age, Store.Debt = POSITION, VELOCITY, AGE, DEBT
Store.TimeScale, Store.Mark, Store.Source, Store.Flags = SCALE, MARK, SOURCE, FLAGS

local DEAD, DIRTY, SPAWN_STREAMED, SYNCED, VISUALIZE, BEAM = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32
Store.Dead, Store.Dirty, Store.SpawnStreamed, Store.Synced, Store.Visualize, Store.Beam =
	DEAD, DIRTY, SPAWN_STREAMED, SYNCED, VISUALIZE, BEAM

local readf32, writef32, readf64, writef64 = buffer.readf32, buffer.writef32, buffer.readf64, buffer.writef64
local readu8, writeu8, readu32, writeu32 = buffer.readu8, buffer.writeu8, buffer.readu32, buffer.writeu32
local band, bor, bnot = bit32.band, bit32.bor, bit32.bnot

local capacity = 1024
Store.data = buffer.create(capacity * STRIDE)
Store.Generation = {} :: { number } -- [slot] = times released
local used = 0 -- slots ever handed out
local free: { number } = {}

-- Sources (the shooter Entity), shared by many projectiles: [index] = source.
Store.Sources = {} :: { any }
local sourceIndex: { [any]: number } = {}
local sourceRefs: { number } = {}
local freeSources: { number } = {}

-- Hot fields and their kind.
local HOT: { [string]: number } = {
	Position = 1, Velocity = 2, Age = 3, _simulationDebt = 4, TimeScale = 5,
	Dead = 6, _spawnStreamed = 7, _streamedSynced = 8, _sweepMark = 9,
}
Store.HotFields = HOT
local MOTION_LAST = 6 -- kinds 1..6 mark the record Dirty when written

local NAN = 0 / 0
local BAD_POSITION = Vector3.new(NAN, NAN, NAN) -- fails isFiniteVector, so Step expires it

local function readVector(b: buffer, o: number): Vector3
	return Vector3.new(readf32(b, o), readf32(b, o + 4), readf32(b, o + 8))
end

local function writeVector(b: buffer, o: number, v: Vector3)
	writef32(b, o, v.X)
	writef32(b, o + 4, v.Y)
	writef32(b, o + 8, v.Z)
end

local function flag(b: buffer, o: number, bitValue: number, on: boolean)
	local flags = readu8(b, o + FLAGS)
	writeu8(b, o + FLAGS, if on then bor(flags, bitValue) else band(flags, bnot(bitValue)))
end

local function read(slot: number, kind: number): any
	local b, o = Store.data, slot * STRIDE
	if kind == 1 then
		return readVector(b, o + POSITION)
	elseif kind == 2 then
		return readVector(b, o + VELOCITY)
	elseif kind == 3 then
		return readf64(b, o + AGE)
	elseif kind == 4 then
		return readf64(b, o + DEBT)
	elseif kind == 5 then
		return readf64(b, o + SCALE)
	elseif kind == 6 then
		return band(readu8(b, o + FLAGS), DEAD) ~= 0
	elseif kind == 7 then
		return band(readu8(b, o + FLAGS), SPAWN_STREAMED) ~= 0
	elseif kind == 8 then
		return band(readu8(b, o + FLAGS), SYNCED) ~= 0
	end
	return readf64(b, o + MARK)
end

local function write(slot: number, kind: number, value: any)
	local b, o = Store.data, slot * STRIDE
	if kind == 1 then
		writeVector(b, o + POSITION, if typeof(value) == "Vector3" then value else BAD_POSITION)
	elseif kind == 2 then
		-- (Step turns a non-vector Velocity into zero; same here)
		writeVector(b, o + VELOCITY, if typeof(value) == "Vector3" then value else Vector3.zero)
	elseif kind == 3 then
		writef64(b, o + AGE, tonumber(value) or 0)
	elseif kind == 4 then
		writef64(b, o + DEBT, tonumber(value) or 0)
	elseif kind == 5 then
		writef64(b, o + SCALE, if type(value) == "number" then value else 1)
	elseif kind == 6 then
		flag(b, o, DEAD, value == true)
	elseif kind == 7 then
		flag(b, o, SPAWN_STREAMED, value == true)
	elseif kind == 8 then
		flag(b, o, SYNCED, value == true)
	else
		writef64(b, o + MARK, tonumber(value) or 0)
	end
	if kind <= MOTION_LAST then
		flag(b, o, DIRTY, true)
	end
end

local function allocate(): number
	local slot = table.remove(free)
	if slot then
		return slot
	end
	slot = used
	used += 1
	if used > capacity then
		local grown = buffer.create(capacity * 2 * STRIDE)
		buffer.copy(grown, 0, Store.data, 0, capacity * STRIDE)
		capacity *= 2
		Store.data = grown
	end
	Store.Generation[slot] = 0
	return slot
end

local function addSource(source: any): number
	if source == nil then
		return 0
	end
	local index = sourceIndex[source]
	if not index then
		index = table.remove(freeSources) or #Store.Sources + 1
		sourceIndex[source] = index
		Store.Sources[index] = source
		sourceRefs[index] = 0
	end
	sourceRefs[index] += 1
	return index
end

local function dropSource(index: number)
	if index == 0 then
		return
	end
	sourceRefs[index] -= 1
	if sourceRefs[index] == 0 then
		sourceIndex[Store.Sources[index]] = nil
		Store.Sources[index] = nil
		table.insert(freeSources, index)
	end
end

-- The metatable live projectiles get: hot fields go to the record, anything
-- else is an ordinary field (or a method from `class`).
function Store.Metatable(class: any): any
	return {
		__index = function(self: any, key: any): any
			local kind = HOT[key]
			if kind then
				return read(self._slot, kind)
			end
			return class[key]
		end,
		__newindex = function(self: any, key: any, value: any)
			local kind = HOT[key]
			if kind then
				write(self._slot, kind, value)
			else
				rawset(self, key, value)
			end
		end,
	}
end

-- Moves a new projectile table's hot fields into a fresh record and gives it
-- `metatable` (from Store.Metatable). Returns the table.
function Store.Adopt(state: any, metatable: any): any
	local slot = allocate()
	local b, o = Store.data, slot * STRIDE
	buffer.fill(b, o, 0, STRIDE)
	for key, kind in HOT do
		local value = rawget(state, key)
		rawset(state, key, nil)
		write(slot, kind, value)
	end
	local flags = band(readu8(b, o + FLAGS), bnot(DIRTY))
	if state.Visualize then
		flags = bor(flags, VISUALIZE)
	end
	if state.Beam ~= nil then
		flags = bor(flags, BEAM)
	end
	writeu8(b, o + FLAGS, flags)
	writeu32(b, o + SOURCE, addSource(state.Source))
	rawset(state, "_slot", slot)
	return setmetatable(state, metatable)
end

-- Copies a projectile's hot fields back into its table as plain fields,
-- gives it `metatable` (the class) and frees its record. No-op if it has none.
function Store.Release(state: any, metatable: any)
	local slot = rawget(state, "_slot")
	if not slot then
		return
	end
	dropSource(readu32(Store.data, slot * STRIDE + SOURCE))
	setmetatable(state, metatable)
	rawset(state, "_slot", nil)
	for key, kind in HOT do
		rawset(state, key, read(slot, kind))
	end
	Store.Generation[slot] += 1
	table.insert(free, slot)
end

-- A plain copy of a projectile (live or released): its fields, hot ones
-- included, with no record and no metatable -- ready for Adopt.
function Store.CloneRaw(state: any): any
	local copy = table.clone(state)
	setmetatable(copy, nil)
	local slot = rawget(state, "_slot")
	if slot then
		for key, kind in HOT do
			rawset(copy, key, read(slot, kind))
		end
		rawset(copy, "_slot", nil)
	end
	return copy
end

function Store.ClearDirty(slot: number)
	flag(Store.data, slot * STRIDE, DIRTY, false)
end

-- Live slots (for the Stats tab).
function Store.Count(): number
	return used - #free
end

return Store
-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/server/Projectile/Store.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/Sweep.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!strict
--!native
--!optimize 2
--[[
	Projectile/Sweep.luau
	The parallel half of projectile movement: the substep loop of
	Projectile.Step for a projectile with no homing and no lag compensation,
	run inside an Actor worker (ProjectileWorkerBootstrap) on a packed copy of
	its state. It plans, casts and integrates exactly as Step does -- same
	ProjectileMotion / ProjectileStepPlanner calls, same constants -- and stops
	at the first contact, handing that substep (and everything after it) back
	to the serial Step code, which owns hits, damage and signals. So a frame
	with no contact is computed entirely here; one with a contact ends in the
	same state it would have without the split.

	Also defines the packed layouts both sides use:
	  input  (48 bytes): motion spec id u32, filter id u32, position 3 x f32,
	         velocity 3 x f32 (Vector3s are float32: exact), age f64,
	         remaining f64. The per-shot constants (acceleration and its
	         direction, gravity, min/max speed, radius, lifetime) are a
	         MotionSpec the workers are sent once and keep, like filters.
	  output (OUTPUT_BYTES): status u8, guard u8, position 3 x f32, velocity
	         3 x f32 (both are Vector3s, float32 already: exact), age f64,
	         remaining f64
]]

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local Shared = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Shared")
local ProjectileMotion = require(Shared:WaitForChild("ProjectileMotion"))
local Planner = require(Shared:WaitForChild("ProjectileStepPlanner"))

local Sweep = {}

Sweep.MaxSubsteps = 16
Sweep.Done = 0 -- loop finished; `remaining` is the carried simulation debt
Sweep.Contact = 1 -- the next substep hits something: resume serially from here
Sweep.Expired = 2 -- lifetime ran out (Step returns false)

local MIN_STEP_DT = ProjectileMotion.MinStepDt
local MAX_SUBSTEPS = Sweep.MaxSubsteps
local DONE, CONTACT, EXPIRED = Sweep.Done, Sweep.Contact, Sweep.Expired

local IN, OUT = 48, 44

-- Byte strides and offsets Parallel's persistent slots update in place.
Sweep.InputStride, Sweep.OutputStride = IN, OUT
Sweep.InputMotion = 8 -- position then velocity, 6 x f32 (same layout as the output's)
Sweep.InputAge = 32
Sweep.InputRemaining = 40
-- output offsets
Sweep.OutStatus, Sweep.OutGuard, Sweep.OutPosition, Sweep.OutVelocity, Sweep.OutAge, Sweep.OutRemaining =
	0, 1, 4, 16, 28, 36

-- A projectile's per-shot motion constants, as the workers keep them.
export type MotionSpec = {
	Acceleration: number | Vector3,
	Direction: Vector3?,
	Gravity: number | Vector3,
	MinSpeed: number,
	MaxSpeed: number,
	Radius: number,
	Lifetime: number,
}

local writef64, readf64 = buffer.writef64, buffer.readf64
local writef32, readf32, writeu8, readu8 = buffer.writef32, buffer.readf32, buffer.writeu8, buffer.readu8
local writeu32, readu32 = buffer.writeu32, buffer.readu32

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Packing
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

function Sweep.InputSize(count: number): number
	return count * IN
end

function Sweep.OutputSize(count: number): number
	return count * OUT
end

local function writeVector32(b: buffer, offset: number, v: Vector3)
	writef32(b, offset, v.X)
	writef32(b, offset + 4, v.Y)
	writef32(b, offset + 8, v.Z)
end

local function readVector32(b: buffer, offset: number): Vector3
	return Vector3.new(readf32(b, offset), readf32(b, offset + 4), readf32(b, offset + 8))
end

-- The motion spec of `p` (its per-shot constants; see MotionSpec).
function Sweep.SpecOf(p: any): MotionSpec
	return {
		Acceleration = p.Acceleration or 0,
		Direction = p.AccelerationDirection,
		Gravity = p.Gravity or 0,
		MinSpeed = p.MinSpeed,
		MaxSpeed = p.MaxSpeed,
		Radius = p.Radius,
		Lifetime = p.Lifetime,
	}
end

function Sweep.WriteInput(b: buffer, item: number, spec: number, filter: number, p: any, remaining: number)
	local o = (item - 1) * IN
	writeu32(b, o, spec)
	writeu32(b, o + 4, filter)
	writeVector32(b, o + 8, p.Position)
	writeVector32(b, o + 20, p.Velocity)
	writef64(b, o + 32, p.Age)
	writef64(b, o + 40, remaining)
end

function Sweep.WriteOutput(b: buffer, item: number, status: number, position: Vector3, velocity: Vector3, age: number, remaining: number, guard: number)
	local o = (item - 1) * OUT
	writeu8(b, o, status)
	writeu8(b, o + 1, guard)
	writeVector32(b, o + 4, position)
	writeVector32(b, o + 16, velocity)
	writef64(b, o + 28, age)
	writef64(b, o + 36, remaining)
end

-- One result as plain values (no table): status, position, velocity, age,
-- remaining, guard.
function Sweep.ReadOutputValues(b: buffer, item: number): (number, Vector3, Vector3, number, number, number)
	local o = (item - 1) * OUT
	return readu8(b, o), readVector32(b, o + 4), readVector32(b, o + 16), readf64(b, o + 28),
		readf64(b, o + 36), readu8(b, o + 1)
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The loop
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Runs one packed projectile and writes its result. `specs` are the motion
-- specs this worker has been sent; `castHits(from, displacement, radius,
-- filter)` is the worker's movement cast (occupancy skip +
-- Raycast/Spherecast); `hasEntities(position)` its mirror of
-- Raycast.chunkHasEntities.
function Sweep.Run(
	input: buffer,
	item: number,
	output: buffer,
	uniformTime: boolean,
	specs: { [number]: MotionSpec },
	castHits: (Vector3, Vector3, number, number) -> boolean,
	hasEntities: (Vector3) -> boolean
)
	local o = (item - 1) * IN
	local filter = readu32(input, o + 4)
	local position = readVector32(input, o + 8)
	local velocity = readVector32(input, o + 20)
	local age = readf64(input, o + 32)
	local remaining = readf64(input, o + 40)
	local spec = specs[readu32(input, o)]
	if not spec then
		-- unknown spec: hand the whole frame to the serial path
		Sweep.WriteOutput(output, item, CONTACT, position, velocity, age, remaining, 0)
		return
	end
	local acceleration, direction, gravity = spec.Acceleration, spec.Direction, spec.Gravity
	local minSpeed, maxSpeed, radius, lifetime = spec.MinSpeed, spec.MaxSpeed, spec.Radius, spec.Lifetime

	-- Mirrors Projectile.Step's loop (no homing: maxDt is unbounded; no
	-- rewind: no lag-compensated entity check).
	local guard = 0
	while remaining > MIN_STEP_DT and guard < MAX_SUBSTEPS do
		guard += 1
		local lifeRemaining = lifetime - age
		if lifeRemaining <= MIN_STEP_DT then
			Sweep.WriteOutput(output, item, EXPIRED, position, velocity, age, remaining, guard)
			return
		end

		local accelerationVector = ProjectileMotion.GetAcceleration(velocity, acceleration, direction, gravity)
		local sample, chunkScale = Planner.Sample(position, velocity, accelerationVector, uniformTime)
		if chunkScale <= 0 then
			remaining = 0
			break
		end
		local highRes = hasEntities(sample)
		local stepDt = Planner.StepDt(position, velocity, accelerationVector, chunkScale, remaining, lifeRemaining,
			highRes, uniformTime, math.huge)
		if stepDt <= 0 then
			break
		end

		local endVelocity, movementVelocity = ProjectileMotion.Integrate(velocity, acceleration, direction, gravity,
			minSpeed, maxSpeed, stepDt)
		local displacement = movementVelocity * stepDt
		if castHits(position, displacement, radius, filter) then
			-- hand this substep back untouched; Step redoes it serially
			Sweep.WriteOutput(output, item, CONTACT, position, velocity, age, remaining, guard - 1)
			return
		end
		velocity = endVelocity
		position += displacement
		age += stepDt
		remaining -= stepDt / chunkScale
		if age >= lifetime - MIN_STEP_DT then
			Sweep.WriteOutput(output, item, EXPIRED, position, velocity, age, remaining, guard)
			return
		end
	end
	Sweep.WriteOutput(output, item, DONE, position, velocity, age, remaining, guard)
end

return Sweep
-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/server/Projectile/Sweep.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/Profile.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!strict
--!native
--!optimize 2
--[[
	Projectile/Profile.luau
	Where the main thread's projectile time goes, for the debug panel's Stats
	tab: named sections accumulate seconds, and Take() returns each as average
	ms per frame since the last call.

	Per-projectile parts are SAMPLED (one projectile in SAMPLE is timed and the
	result scaled up) so the timer calls don't distort the very loops being
	measured; those sections are estimates, labelled as such in the Stats tab.
]]

local Profile = {}

Profile.SAMPLE = 32 -- time one projectile in this many in per-projectile loops

local totals: { [string]: number } = {}
local counts: { [string]: number } = {}
local frames = 0

function Profile.Add(name: string, seconds: number)
	totals[name] = (totals[name] or 0) + seconds
end

-- A per-frame count (reported as the average per frame, not ms).
function Profile.Count(name: string, n: number)
	counts[name] = (counts[name] or 0) + n
end

-- Lua heap at the last frame, and how much the garbage collector freed
-- since the last Take (heap drops between frames).
local lastHeap = gcinfo()
local freedKB = 0

-- One server frame passed (called once per projectile Heartbeat step).
function Profile.Frame()
	frames += 1
	local heap = gcinfo()
	if heap < lastHeap then
		freedKB += lastHeap - heap
	end
	lastHeap = heap
end

-- { [section] = average ms per frame, [count] = average per frame } since
-- the last call, then resets.
function Profile.Take(): { [string]: number }
	local result = {}
	local count = math.max(frames, 1)
	for name, seconds in totals do
		result[name] = seconds / count * 1000
	end
	for name, n in counts do
		result[name] = n / count
	end
	result.HeapMB = lastHeap / 1024
	result.GcFreedMB = freedKB / 1024 / count
	freedKB = 0
	table.clear(totals)
	table.clear(counts)
	frames = 0
	return result
end

return Profile
-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/server/Projectile/Profile.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/Parallel.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!strict
--!native
--!optimize 2
--[[
	Projectile/Parallel.luau
	Main-thread side of parallel projectile movement.

	Each worker Actor owns a batch of SLOTS. A slot holds one projectile's
	packed movement record (Sweep's input layout) and what the projectile
	looked like after the last frame, and it persists across frames: a
	projectile that just flies is packed once, and from then on its record is
	updated straight from the worker's output. Together with Store.luau (the
	projectile's own hot fields in a buffer), a projectile that just flies
	costs the main thread only buffer reads and writes per frame -- its table
	(at tens of thousands of projectiles, mostly cache misses) isn't touched.

	  Offer()                 a projectile that stepped serially (or was just
	                          made) asks for a slot; it's queued.
	  PreSimulation (serial)  Dispatch(): queued projectiles that are eligible --
	                          no homing, no lag compensation, not frozen,
	                          finite state, raycast filter already known to the
	                          workers -- are packed into the emptiest batch;
	                          then every slot's step budget is written and each
	                          batch is sent off.
	  parallel phase          workers (ProjectileWorkerBootstrap) run Sweep.Run:
	                          plan, cast, integrate, stop at the first contact.
	  Heartbeat (serial)      Apply(): a plain "moved, hit nothing" result for a
	                          projectile nothing touched is written straight
	                          into its Store record and its slot. Anything else
	                          goes to Projectile's applier (the serial code),
	                          which answers Refresh (repack, or release if no
	                          longer eligible) or Drop (dead: release). A late
	                          batch is released whole.

	Anything changed behind a slot's back (an ability moved it, a time scale
	changed...) shows up as the record's Dirty flag or a different scale, and
	the projectile is stepped serially -- so the slot never has to be told.

	Workers mirror what they need: time scales/zones (sent when
	ChunkManager.GetTimeVersion changes), raycast filters (sent once per
	distinct filter, usable from the next frame), and which chunks hold
	entities (with every batch). Each bakes its own Occupancy.

	Worker raycasts run in the parallel phase that follows PreSimulation, i.e.
	against the world as it was before this frame's physics step; the serial
	path casts after it. Static geometry is identical; moving parts can differ
	by one physics step.
]]

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")

local Shared = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Shared")
local ChunkManager = require(Shared:WaitForChild("ChunkManager"))
local Sweep = require(script.Parent.Sweep)
local Store = require(script.Parent.Store)
local Profile = require(script.Parent.Profile)
local SafeMath = require(Shared:WaitForChild("SafeMath"))

local Parallel = {}

Parallel.Enabled = true
Parallel.MinProjectiles = 32 -- below this, dispatch overhead isn't worth it

-- What an applier returns for a result (see Parallel.Apply).
Parallel.Drop = 0 -- dead: release the slot
Parallel.Refresh = 2 -- alive, but the serial code finished the frame: repack or release
local REFRESH = Parallel.Refresh

-- projectile._parallelState
local QUEUED, SLOTTED = 1, 2

local IN, OUT = Sweep.InputStride, Sweep.OutputStride
local IN_MOTION = Sweep.InputMotion
local OUT_STATUS, OUT_POSITION, OUT_VELOCITY = Sweep.OutStatus, Sweep.OutPosition, Sweep.OutVelocity
local OUT_AGE, OUT_REMAINING = Sweep.OutAge, Sweep.OutRemaining
local IN_AGE, IN_REMAINING = Sweep.InputAge, Sweep.InputRemaining
local MIN_CAPACITY = 64
local readf64, writef64, readf32, writef32, bufferCopy = buffer.readf64, buffer.writef64, buffer.readf32, buffer.writef32, buffer.copy
local readu8, readu32, writeu8, band = buffer.readu8, buffer.readu32, buffer.writeu8, bit32.band
local STRIDE = Store.Stride
local S_POSITION, S_VELOCITY, S_AGE, S_DEBT = Store.Position, Store.Velocity, Store.Age, Store.Debt
local S_SCALE, S_MARK, S_SOURCE, S_FLAGS = Store.TimeScale, Store.Mark, Store.Source, Store.Flags
local DEAD_OR_DIRTY = bit32.bor(Store.Dead, Store.Dirty)
local SWEEP_DONE = Sweep.Done
local LIMIT = SafeMath.Limit
local abs = math.abs

type Worker = { Actor: Actor, Id: number }
-- A worker's latest result, as fired through ProjectileActors.Results.
type Result = { Frame: number, Count: number, Ms: number, Data: buffer?, Checks: number, Skipped: number }
local results: { [number]: Result } = {} -- worker id -> latest

-- Receives a result Apply can't take directly and says what happens to its
-- slot (Refresh or Drop): the projectile, the result (status, position,
-- velocity, age, remaining, guard), whether it was changed since it was
-- packed (Dirty), the scale it was sent with, and the dispatch's time version
-- and uniform-time flag.
export type Applier = (projectile: any, status: number, position: Vector3, velocity: Vector3, age: number,
	remaining: number, guard: number, dirty: boolean, fromScale: number, timeVersion: number,
	uniform: boolean) -> number

-- A worker's slots, item 1..Count (compact: released slots are swap-removed).
type Batch = {
	Count: number,
	Sent: number, -- items dispatched this frame (0: nothing to apply)
	Capacity: number,
	Input: buffer,
	Projectiles: { any },
	Slot: { number }, -- its Store record
	Generation: { number }, -- Store.Generation[slot] when packed (a mismatch: released since)
	Scale: { number },
	Deadline: { number }, -- os.clock() past which MaxRealLifetime is up
}

local workers: { Worker } = {}
local frame = 0
local sentTimeVersion = -1
local filterIds: { [any]: any } = {} -- instance trie -> { [flags]: id }
local filterReady: { [number]: number } = {} -- id -> first frame workers have it
local nextFilterId = 0
local specIds: { [any]: any } = {} -- trie of motion-spec values -> id
local specReady: { [number]: number } = {} -- id -> first frame workers have it
local nextSpecId = 0
local MAX_SPECS = 65535 -- past this many distinct specs, new ones just step serially
local batches: { Batch } = {}
local batchUniform = true
local batchTimeVersion = 0
local running = false -- the last Dispatch sent batches
local queue: { any } = {}
local scaleOf: (any) -> number? = function()
	return nil
end
local released: { number } = {} -- scratch for Apply
local deferred: { number } = {} -- scratch for Apply

local stats = { Parallel = 0, Resumed = 0, Serial = 0, Fallback = 0, Late = 0, Frames = 0, SlowestWorkerMs = 0, WorkerMs = 0,
	AppliedFrames = 0, WorkerChecks = 0, WorkerSkipped = 0 }

local function refreshWorkers()
	if #workers > 0 then
		return
	end
	local root = ServerScriptService:FindFirstChild("ProjectileActors", true)
	local event = root and root:FindFirstChild("Results")
	if not root or not event then
		return
	end
	for _, child in root:GetChildren() do
		local id = tonumber(string.match(child.Name, "(%d+)$"))
		if child:IsA("Actor") and id then
			table.insert(workers, { Actor = child, Id = id })
		end
	end
	if #workers == 0 then
		return
	end
	(event :: BindableEvent).Event:Connect(function(id: number, resultFrame: number, count: number, ms: number,
		data: buffer, checks: number, skipped: number)
		local result = results[id]
		if not result then
			result = { Frame = 0, Count = 0, Ms = 0, Data = nil, Checks = 0, Skipped = 0 }
			results[id] = result
		end
		result.Frame, result.Count, result.Ms, result.Data = resultFrame, count, ms, data
		stats.WorkerChecks += checks
		stats.WorkerSkipped += skipped
	end)
	table.sort(workers, function(a, b)
		return a.Actor.Name < b.Actor.Name
	end)
end

-- Filter id for a projectile's movement RaycastParams, by content (beam
-- samples rebuild identical params per packet). New ids are sent to every
-- worker and become usable next frame.
local filterByParams: { [RaycastParams]: number } = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" }) :: any

local function filterFor(projectile: any): number?
	local cached = projectile._filterId
	if cached then
		return if filterReady[cached] and filterReady[cached] <= frame then cached else nil
	end
	local params: RaycastParams = projectile._rayParams
	-- params are shared between projectiles (Raycast.buildRayParams), so most
	-- lookups end here, without reading FilterDescendantsInstances back
	local known = filterByParams[params]
	if known then
		projectile._filterId = known
		return if filterReady[known] <= frame then known else nil
	end
	local instances = params.FilterDescendantsInstances
	local node = filterIds
	for _, instance in instances do
		local nextNode = node[instance]
		if not nextNode then
			nextNode = {}
			node[instance] = nextNode
		end
		node = nextNode
	end
	local flags = `{params.IgnoreWater}|{params.CollisionGroup}`
	local id = node[flags]
	if not id then
		nextFilterId += 1
		id = nextFilterId
		node[flags] = id
		filterReady[id] = frame + 1
		for _, worker in workers do
			worker.Actor:SendMessage("Filter", id, instances, params.IgnoreWater, params.CollisionGroup)
		end
	end
	projectile._filterId = id
	filterByParams[params] = id
	return if filterReady[id] <= frame then id else nil
end

local function syncTimeWorld()
	local version = ChunkManager.GetTimeVersion()
	if version == sentTimeVersion then
		return
	end
	sentTimeVersion = version
	local chunks = {}
	for _, chunk in ChunkManager.GetAllChunks() do
		if chunk.TimeScale ~= 1 then
			table.insert(chunks, { Key = chunk.Key, Scale = chunk.TimeScale })
		end
	end
	local zones = {}
	for _, zone in ChunkManager.GetTimeScaleZones() do
		table.insert(zones, { Id = zone.Id, Position = zone.Position, Radius = zone.Radius, Scale = zone.Scale })
	end
	for _, worker in workers do
		worker.Actor:SendMessage("TimeWorld", ChunkManager.ChunkSize, ChunkManager.UseY, chunks, zones)
	end
end

local function entityChunkKeys(): { Vector3 }
	local keys = {}
	for _, chunk in ChunkManager.GetAllChunks() do
		if chunk.EntityCount > 0 then
			table.insert(keys, chunk.Key)
		end
	end
	return keys
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Slots
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local function newBatch(): Batch
	return {
		Count = 0, Sent = 0, Capacity = MIN_CAPACITY, Input = buffer.create(Sweep.InputSize(MIN_CAPACITY)),
		Projectiles = {}, Slot = {}, Generation = {}, Scale = {}, Deadline = {},
	}
end

-- Resizes a batch's input buffer, keeping its records.
local function resize(batch: Batch, capacity: number)
	local input = buffer.create(Sweep.InputSize(capacity))
	bufferCopy(input, 0, batch.Input, 0, batch.Count * IN)
	batch.Input, batch.Capacity = input, capacity
end

-- Packs `projectile` into slot `item` (new or reused) with its current state.
local function pack(batch: Batch, item: number, projectile: any, filter: number, spec: number, scale: number)
	local slot = projectile._slot
	batch.Projectiles[item] = projectile
	batch.Slot[item] = slot
	batch.Generation[item] = Store.Generation[slot]
	batch.Scale[item] = scale
	batch.Deadline[item] = projectile._spawnRealTime + projectile.MaxRealLifetime
	-- (remaining holds the carried debt until dispatch adds the frame's budget)
	Sweep.WriteInput(batch.Input, item, spec, filter, projectile, projectile._simulationDebt)
	Store.ClearDirty(slot)
end

-- Motion spec id for a projectile's per-shot constants (see
-- Sweep.MotionSpec), by value; new ids are sent to every worker and become
-- usable next frame. nil if not usable yet (or the values can't be keys).
local NIL = newproxy()
local values = table.create(7) -- scratch
local function specFor(projectile: any): number?
	local node = specIds
	values[1], values[2], values[3] = projectile.Acceleration or 0, projectile.AccelerationDirection, projectile.Gravity or 0
	values[4], values[5], values[6], values[7] = projectile.MinSpeed, projectile.MaxSpeed, projectile.Radius, projectile.Lifetime
	for index = 1, 7 do
		local value = values[index]
		if value == nil then
			value = NIL
		elseif value ~= value then
			return nil -- NaN can't be a key; the serial path deals with it
		end
		local nextNode = node[value]
		if not nextNode then
			if index == 7 then
				if nextSpecId >= MAX_SPECS then
					return nil
				end
				nextSpecId += 1
				nextNode = nextSpecId
				specReady[nextNode] = frame + 1
				local spec = Sweep.SpecOf(projectile)
				for _, worker in workers do
					worker.Actor:SendMessage("Motion", nextNode, spec)
				end
			else
				nextNode = {}
			end
			node[value] = nextNode
		end
		node = nextNode
	end
	local id = node :: any
	return if specReady[id] <= frame then id else nil
end

-- Its scale, filter id and motion spec id if it may have a slot right now,
-- else nil.
local function eligible(projectile: any): (number?, number?, number?)
	if not projectile._slot then
		return nil, nil, nil -- (released: it's gone)
	end
	local scale = scaleOf(projectile)
	if not scale then
		return nil, nil, nil
	end
	local filter = projectile._filterId
	if not filter or filterReady[filter] > frame then
		filter = filterFor(projectile)
	end
	return scale, filter, specFor(projectile)
end

-- Swap-removes slot `item`.
local function release(batch: Batch, item: number)
	local last = batch.Count
	local projectiles = batch.Projectiles
	projectiles[item]._parallelState = nil
	if item ~= last then
		local input = batch.Input
		local o = (item - 1) * IN
		bufferCopy(input, o, input, (last - 1) * IN, IN)
		projectiles[item] = projectiles[last]
		batch.Slot[item] = batch.Slot[last]
		batch.Generation[item] = batch.Generation[last]
		batch.Scale[item] = batch.Scale[last]
		batch.Deadline[item] = batch.Deadline[last]
	end
	projectiles[last] = nil
	batch.Count = last - 1
end

local function releaseBatch(batch: Batch)
	local projectiles = batch.Projectiles
	for item = 1, batch.Count do
		projectiles[item]._parallelState = nil
		projectiles[item] = nil
	end
	batch.Count, batch.Sent = 0, 0
end

-- Empties every slot and the queue (parallel movement paused or off).
local function releaseAll()
	for _, batch in batches do
		releaseBatch(batch)
	end
	for _, projectile in queue do
		projectile._parallelState = nil
	end
	table.clear(queue)
end

-- `fn(projectile)`: its combined time scale when it may move in parallel,
-- else nil. Called when a projectile is packed or repacked.
function Parallel.SetEligibility(fn: (any) -> number?)
	scaleOf = fn
end

-- Asks for a slot for `projectile` (call after it stepped serially or was
-- created). Packed at the next Dispatch if it's still eligible then.
function Parallel.Offer(projectile: any)
	if running and not projectile._parallelState then
		projectile._parallelState = QUEUED
		table.insert(queue, projectile)
	end
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Frame
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Packs queued projectiles and sends this frame's batches. `allowed` false
-- (e.g. debug rays on) pauses parallel movement: every slot is released and
-- everything steps serially.
function Parallel.Dispatch(activeCount: number, globalDt: number, allowed: boolean)
	local clock = os.clock
	local setupStarted = clock()
	for _, batch in batches do
		batch.Sent = 0
	end
	refreshWorkers()
	local workerCount = #workers
	running = Parallel.Enabled and allowed and workerCount > 0 and activeCount >= Parallel.MinProjectiles and globalDt > 0
	if not running then
		releaseAll()
		return
	end
	frame += 1
	syncTimeWorld()
	batchTimeVersion = ChunkManager.GetTimeVersion()
	batchUniform = ChunkManager.IsTimeUniform()
	for w = 1, workerCount do
		local batch = batches[w]
		if not batch then
			batches[w] = newBatch()
		elseif batch.Capacity > MIN_CAPACITY and batch.Count * 4 < batch.Capacity then
			-- (the whole buffer is copied to the worker each frame)
			resize(batch, math.max(MIN_CAPACITY, batch.Count * 2))
		end
	end

	-- the queue: into the emptiest batch
	local acquireStarted = clock()
	local acquired = 0
	for _, projectile in queue do
		projectile._parallelState = nil
		if projectile.Dead then
			continue
		end
		local scale, filter, spec = eligible(projectile)
		if not scale or not filter or not spec then
			continue
		end
		local batch = batches[1]
		for w = 2, workerCount do
			if batches[w].Count < batch.Count then
				batch = batches[w]
			end
		end
		local item = batch.Count + 1
		if item > batch.Capacity then
			resize(batch, batch.Capacity * 2)
		end
		batch.Count = item
		pack(batch, item, projectile, filter, spec, scale)
		projectile._parallelState = SLOTTED
		acquired += 1
	end
	table.clear(queue)

	-- this frame's step budget for every slot: its record's remaining field
	-- holds the carried debt (written by pack and Apply), so this is a
	-- sequential pass over each batch
	local loopStarted = clock()
	for w = 1, workerCount do
		local batch = batches[w]
		local input, scales = batch.Input, batch.Scale
		for item = 1, batch.Count do
			local o = (item - 1) * IN + IN_REMAINING
			writef64(input, o, globalDt * scales[item] + readf64(input, o))
		end
	end

	local sendStarted = clock()
	local keys = entityChunkKeys()
	local slots = 0
	for w = 1, workerCount do
		local batch = batches[w]
		local count = batch.Count
		slots += count
		if count > 0 then
			batch.Sent = count
			workers[w].Actor:SendMessage("Sweep", frame, batch.Input, count, batchUniform, keys)
		end
	end
	stats.Frames += 1
	Profile.Add("DispatchSetup", acquireStarted - setupStarted)
	Profile.Add("DispatchAcquire", loopStarted - acquireStarted)
	Profile.Add("DispatchLoop", sendStarted - loopStarted)
	Profile.Add("DispatchSend", clock() - sendStarted)
	Profile.Count("Slots", slots)
	Profile.Count("Acquired", acquired)
end

-- Pass 1 of Apply: every result that is a plain "moved, hit nothing" for a
-- projectile nothing touched is written straight into its Store record and
-- its slot's packed record; the rest go into `deferred` (and released slots
-- into `released`). Its own function, with typed buffers, so the native
-- compiler specialises every buffer access. Returns dropped, deferred, kept.
local function applyPlain(store: buffer, data: buffer, input: buffer, count: number, slots: { number },
	generations: { number }, scales: { number }, deadlines: { number }, generationOf: { number },
	sources: { any }, now: number, mark: number): (number, number, number)
	local dropped, slow, kept = 0, 0, 0
	for item = 1, count do
		local slot = slots[item]
		if generationOf[slot] ~= generations[item] then
			-- released since (the step loop dropped it): nothing to apply
			dropped += 1
			released[dropped] = item
			continue
		end
		local o = slot * STRIDE
		local out = (item - 1) * OUT
		local plain = readu8(data, out + OUT_STATUS) == SWEEP_DONE and band(readu8(store, o + S_FLAGS), DEAD_OR_DIRTY) == 0
			and now < deadlines[item]
		if plain then
			-- its scale is still the one it was sent with (own * source's; anything
			-- unusual goes to the serial code, which uses combinedTimeScale)
			local own = readf64(store, o + S_SCALE)
			local index = readu32(store, o + S_SOURCE)
			local sourceScale: any = if index ~= 0 then sources[index].TimeScale else 1
			plain = type(sourceScale) == "number" and sourceScale >= 0 and own >= 0 and sourceScale < LIMIT
				and own < LIMIT and sourceScale * own == scales[item]
		end
		if not plain then
			slow += 1
			deferred[slow] = item
			continue
		end
		-- position/velocity are float32 in the output, the record and the slot
		bufferCopy(store, o + S_POSITION, data, out + OUT_POSITION, 24)
		local age = readf64(data, out + OUT_AGE)
		local debt = readf64(data, out + OUT_REMAINING)
		writef64(store, o + S_AGE, age)
		writef64(store, o + S_DEBT, debt)
		local i = (item - 1) * IN
		bufferCopy(input, i + IN_MOTION, data, out + OUT_POSITION, 24)
		writef64(input, i + IN_AGE, age)
		writef64(input, i + IN_REMAINING, debt) -- (dispatch adds next frame's budget)
		local px, py, pz = readf32(data, out + OUT_POSITION), readf32(data, out + OUT_POSITION + 4),
			readf32(data, out + OUT_POSITION + 8)
		if abs(px) <= LIMIT and abs(py) <= LIMIT and abs(pz) <= LIMIT then
			writef64(store, o + S_MARK, mark)
			kept += 1
		else
			-- flew past SafeMath.Limit: dies in the step loop
			writef64(store, o + S_MARK, -mark)
			dropped += 1
			released[dropped] = item
		end
	end
	return dropped, slow, kept
end

-- Applies this frame's results. `mark` is the step loop's frame mark (written
-- into the record of every projectile handled here), `now` its os.clock(),
-- `timeVersion` ChunkManager's current time version. A plain "moved, hit
-- nothing" result for an untouched projectile is written straight into its
-- record and slot; anything else goes to `apply` (see Applier). Batches a
-- worker hasn't finished (or never got) are released -- those projectiles
-- just step serially and are offered again.
function Parallel.Apply(apply: Applier, mark: number, now: number, timeVersion: number)
	local clock = os.clock
	local decodeTime, loopTime, slowTime, releaseTime, releases, kept = 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0
	local transferred = 0
	local slowest, total, any = 0, 0, false
	local sameVersion = timeVersion == batchTimeVersion
	for w, batch in batches do
		local count = batch.Sent
		if count == 0 then
			continue
		end
		batch.Sent = 0
		local worker = workers[w]
		local result = worker and results[worker.Id]
		local data = result and result.Data
		if not result or not data or result.Frame ~= frame or result.Count ~= count then
			stats.Late += count
			releases += batch.Count
			releaseBatch(batch)
			continue
		end
		-- (the event already handed us our own copy of the worker's buffer)
		local decodeStarted = clock()
		result.Data = nil
		local ms = result.Ms
		slowest, total, any = math.max(slowest, ms), total + ms, true
		transferred += buffer.len(data)
		local input = batch.Input
		local projectiles, slots, generations, scales, deadlines =
			batch.Projectiles, batch.Slot, batch.Generation, batch.Scale, batch.Deadline
		local generationOf = Store.Generation
		local loopStarted = clock()
		decodeTime += loopStarted - decodeStarted
		table.clear(released)
		-- Pass 1, buffers only: every plain result for an untouched projectile.
		-- The rest are deferred to pass 2, so the serial code (raycasts,
		-- Step, allocation) doesn't keep evicting this loop's working set.
		local dropped, slow, keptHere = 0, 0, 0
		if sameVersion then
			dropped, slow, keptHere = applyPlain(Store.data, data, input, count, slots, generations, scales, deadlines,
				generationOf, Store.Sources, now, mark)
		else
			for item = 1, count do
				deferred[item] = item
			end
			slow = count
		end
		kept += keptHere

		-- Pass 2: the serial code finishes the rest.
		local slowStarted = clock()
		for index = 1, slow do
			local item = deferred[index]
			local projectile = projectiles[item]
			local status, position, velocity, age, remaining, guard = Sweep.ReadOutputValues(data, item)
			local flags = readu8(Store.data, slots[item] * STRIDE + S_FLAGS)
			local outcome = apply(projectile, status, position, velocity, age, remaining, guard,
				band(flags, Store.Dirty) ~= 0, scales[item], batchTimeVersion, batchUniform)
			local keep = false
			if outcome == REFRESH and not projectile.Dead then
				local scale, filter, spec = eligible(projectile)
				if scale and filter and spec then
					pack(batch, item, projectile, filter, spec, scale)
					keep = true
				end
			end
			if not keep then
				dropped += 1
				released[dropped] = item
			end
		end
		slowTime += clock() - slowStarted
		-- (releases must go highest item first; pass 2 added some out of order)
		if slow > 0 then
			table.sort(released, function(x, y)
				return x < y
			end)
		end
		local releaseStarted = clock()
		loopTime += releaseStarted - loopStarted
		-- backwards, so a swap never moves a slot that's still to be released
		for index = dropped, 1, -1 do
			release(batch, released[index])
		end
		releases += dropped
		releaseTime += clock() - releaseStarted
	end
	stats.Parallel += kept
	Profile.Add("ApplyDecode", decodeTime)
	Profile.Count("TransferKB", transferred / 1024)
	Profile.Add("ApplyLoop", loopTime - slowTime)
	Profile.Add("ApplySlow", slowTime)
	Profile.Add("ApplyRelease", releaseTime)
	Profile.Count("Released", releases)
	if any then
		stats.SlowestWorkerMs += slowest
		stats.WorkerMs += total
		stats.AppliedFrames += 1
	end
end

-- Per-frame totals from the step loop (Resumed: a worker stopped at a contact
-- and the serial code finished the frame).
function Parallel.AddCounts(parallel: number, resumed: number, serial: number, fallback: number)
	stats.Parallel += parallel
	stats.Resumed += resumed
	stats.Serial += serial
	stats.Fallback += fallback
end

-- Counters since the last call, then resets.
function Parallel.TakeStats()
	local snapshot = table.clone(stats)
	snapshot.Workers = #workers
	local frames = math.max(stats.AppliedFrames, 1)
	snapshot.SlowestWorkerMs = stats.SlowestWorkerMs / frames -- per frame, averaged
	snapshot.WorkerMs = stats.WorkerMs / frames
	stats.Parallel, stats.Resumed, stats.Serial, stats.Fallback, stats.Late, stats.Frames = 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0
	stats.WorkerChecks, stats.WorkerSkipped = 0, 0
	stats.SlowestWorkerMs, stats.WorkerMs, stats.AppliedFrames = 0, 0, 0
	return snapshot
end

return Parallel
-- =============================================================================
-- END FILE: src/server/Projectile/Parallel.luau
-- =============================================================================

-- =============================================================================
-- BEGIN FILE: src/server/Projectile/init.luau
-- =============================================================================
--!native
--!strict
--!optimize 2
--[[
	Projectile (server)
	Server-authoritative, raycast-driven projectiles that live in dilated time.
	Every projectile steps in the local time of the chunk it currently occupies,
	so a bullet flying through a 0.2x slow zone crawls, its gravity floats, and
	its fuse burns slower — all for free. Because of that, a dilated Lifetime
	alone can't bound a projectile's real-world lifespan -- something frozen at
	0x (its own TimeScale, its Source's personal ratio, or its chunk) would
	never expire on its own. MaxRealLifetime is a separate, real-time
	(wall-clock) hard cap that always applies regardless of dilation -- see
	DEFAULT_MAX_REAL_LIFETIME / Projectile.SetDefaultMaxRealLifetime below.

	This module lives in ServerScriptService (never replicated to clients) --
	all hit-detection, lag-compensation, homing-acquisition, and damage-
	adjacent logic (raycast filters, penetration math, pierce/damage
	multipliers) stays server-only and unreadable by any client, on purpose.
	The purely cosmetic rendering half lives in ReplicatedStorage.Shared as
	ProjectileClient -- require that from client code, this module from
	server code. The two communicate only over VisualOffload's ProjSpawnBatch /
	ProjMove / ProjHitBatch / ProjSync / ProjTimeScale / ProjRay channels (see
	Projectile/Replication.luau for the sending side).

	Supported behaviours (mix and match): straight shots, ballistic gravity,
	acceleration/deceleration, bouncing (restitution), homing (explicit target or
	auto-acquire by tag(s), with optional Permalock), piercing with falloff, and
	cone bursts. Rendering can be offloaded to clients (Visualize = true): the
	server keeps only the logic. Visuals receive ProjSpawn with their current
	trajectory config and ProjHit on destruction. Finite-range observers also
	receive ProjRangeExit and a fresh authoritative spawn on re-entry; sparse
	corrections must never be lost permanently outside that range.
	On top of that there are three
	independent, orthogonal streaming mechanisms, each covering a different case
	the client can't safely reproduce on its own:
	 - Continuous sync while actively homing (self.HomingTarget ~= nil, checked
	   fresh every tick, never a static classification): the client only ever
	   sees a target's position through that target's own replication lag, which
	   differs per observer, so if it rotated toward that position locally, two
	   clients watching the same missile chase the same target could compute two
	   different flight paths. While a lock is held, the server streams
	   authoritative Position/Velocity through a persistent round-robin batch
	   capped at MAX_SYNC_UPDATES_PER_FRAME. At ordinary counts that is every
	   tick; at stress-test counts each cohort updates on alternating frames.
	   The cursor advances in real frame order and is never reset by dilation,
	   so changing GlobalTimeScale cannot merge staggered cohorts into one spike.
	   A rare ProjSync event tells clients when a visual crosses in or out of
	   continuous-sync mode.
	 - A one-shot correction on every bounce: reproducing a bounce client-side
	   requires matching the server's exact raycast resolution/timing AND
	   knowing which hits are really entities (piercable/filterable, server-only
	   knowledge -- the client has no replicated entity registry to check
	   against), neither of which the client can do reliably. So rather than
	   staying synced for the rest of its life, a bouncing projectile is only
	   ever corrected on the frame it actually bounces: that frame's ProjMove
	   batch carries one entry (Bounced = true) with the contact point and the
	   end-of-frame post-bounce Position/Velocity, which the client snaps to
	   and treats as its new local physics baseline. Between bounces (and
	   before the first one, and after the last one) the client is fully
	   unsynced and coasts on local physics, just like a non-homing,
	   non-bouncing shot.
	 - A one-shot ProjTimeScale message every time a projectile's personal/local
	   dilation actually CHANGES (Source.TimeScale * projectile.TimeScale --
	   see "Local time" below), not a continuous stream: the client can't
	   predict a ratio it's never been told, but once it knows the current
	   number it can fold it straight into the same local ChunkManager.ScaleDt
	   dead-reckoning every unsynced visual already does (see ProjectileClient's
	   render loop), exactly like it already does for chunk/world dilation
	   (which similarly replicates as sparse chunk-scale updates, not a
	   per-projectile stream).
	These three mechanisms are independent and compose freely: a homing
	projectile that also bounces stays continuously synced while locked (the
